Its name was derived from the Latin word xenium, meaning “gift for the guest.” Its design encases both driver and engine in layered carbon fiber and aluminum, resulting in a distinctive wrapped appearance. A V-10 engine has been mounted behind the cockpit, while two electric motors powered the front wheels. To adapt to various terrain conditions, the chassis can be adjusted into four different configurations.
car2119.hero: A high-performance luxury car prepared as a "beautifully wrapped gift."
car2119.nameLong: Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo Street Mode

car2120.desc: This Vision Gran Turismo came from a renowned Italian design house. Its name was derived from the Latin word xenium, meaning “gift for the guest.” Its design encases both driver and engine in layered carbon fiber and aluminum, resulting in a distinctive wrapped appearance. A V-10 engine has been mounted behind the cockpit, while two electric motors powered the front wheels. To adapt to various terrain conditions, the chassis can be adjusted into four different configurations.
car2120.hero: A high-performance luxury car prepared as a "beautifully wrapped gift."
car2120.nameLong: Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo Off-road Mode

car2121.desc: The Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo is a two-seater coupe born from a collaboration between Honda’s design team and Gran Turismo. It embodies Honda’s "Human Centered Design" philosophy, featuring a driver-focused package that prioritized engagement and usability. With bold, athletic proportions, the car delivers the striking presence and excitement expected of a true sports car.
car2121.hero: This lightweight mid-engine sports car embodied Honda's "Power of Dreams" philosophy.

car2122.desc: This Vision Gran Turismo was created by the famed Carrozzeria Zagato, drawing inspiration from the IsoRivolta, a grand tourer produced in the 1960s by the Italian sports-car brand ISO. It inherited the DNA of the IsoRivolta, a car with a rich motorsport history, and reimagined it through the lens of cutting-edge design and modern engineering.
car2122.hero: This Vision Gran Turismo machine pays tribute to the legendary manufacturer, Zagato.

car2123.desc: The Lexus LF-LC GT Vision Gran Turismo is a dream car crafted by Lexus with aspirations for competition in Super GT and the 24 Hours of Nürburgring. Inspired by the LF-LC luxury coupe concept, it merges CALTY DESIGN’s design philosophy with the technical practicality of Lexus Racing.
car2123.hero: A beautiful high performance machine for participation in the Nürburgring 24 hour race.

car2124.desc: The GTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo draws upon the DNA of Volkswagen’s legendary GTI lineage to create a supercar that was both technically advanced and visually striking. Its body, inspired by the iconic Golf silhouette, houses a 502 HP VR6 TSI engine. With a lowered center of gravity and the extensive use of lightweight components, the car exhibits an exceptional handling experience.
car2124.hero: The ultimate GTI; there's a reason this car's name includes "Supersport."
car2124.nameLong: Volkswagen GTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo

car2127.desc: In spring 2014, Nissan announced its return to the 24 Hours of Le Mans with a car bearing the GT-R nameplate. The GT-R LM NISMO broke convention with its radical front-engine/front-wheel-drive layout. Its carbon-fiber body, designed by Ben Bowlby—the mind behind the DeltaWing and ZEOD RC—housed a twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 paired with an energy recovery system. Weighing in at the minimum 1940 lbs, it contended for overall victory on motorsports' most demanding stage.
car2127.hero: A front-wheel-drive prototype hybrid racer designed by Ben Bowlby.

car2131.desc: This was a purpose-built racing machine that began competing in GT events in 2012, continuing the proud legacy established by its predecessors, the DBR9 and DBRS9. Based on the V8 Vantage platform, it featured widened fenders and a prominent rear wing, while its weight was reduced to just 2756 lbs. The V-12 engine was tuned to deliver 591.7 HP and 513.5 ft-lb of torque, paired with an XTrac sequential transmission with paddle shifters. The car would go on to deliver exceptional performances at circuits across the globe.
car2131.hero: A well-balanced, high-performance car that immediately became a familiar presence on race podiums.

car2134.desc: This machine was conceived as a tribute to Bugatti’s storied racing heritage. Designers and engineers collaborated to craft the vehicle using cutting-edge technologies and advanced aerodynamic theory. Powered by a W16 engine with four turbochargers, it produced an astonishing 1230kW and 1580Nm of torque (1649.9 HP/1165.2 ft-lb), enabling it to exceed 248.5 mph in four sections of Circuit de la Sarthe, home of the 24 Hours of Le Mans. This immense power allowed the car to achieve a top speed of 278.1 mph.
car2134.hero: This Vision Gran Turismo machine pays homage to the Type 57 Tank, one of the glorious cars that define Bugatti's history.

car2135.desc: Created to commemorate Hyundai’s 50th anniversary, this model also embodied the spirit and ambition of the company's high-performance "N" division. It was powered by hydrogen fuel cells paired with supercapacitors that stored energy recovered through regenerative braking, delivering a combined output of 650 kW (871.8 HP) via electric motors at each wheel. Thanks to compact, lightweight fuel-cell stacks and a CFRP monocoque chassis, the car tipped the scales at just 2143 lbs.
car2135.hero: An extreme monster machine that embodies the passion and future of Hyundai's "N".

car2136.desc: Alfa Romeo’s first mass-produced mid-engine sports car, the 4C made its debut in 2013. Its design paid tribute to the timeless lines of the Tipo 33/2 Stradale. The 1742 cc 4-cylinder engine, producing 236.7 HP and 253.2 ft-lb of torque, was paired with an exceptionally lightweight body, enabling the car to accelerate from zero to 62.1 mph in just 4.5 seconds and reach a top speed of 160.3 mph. A special "Launch Edition" was also released, limited to just 1,000 units worldwide.
car2136.hero: The launch edition of the 4C, limited to 1000 units, sold out almost immediately after going on sale.

car2138.desc: In 2014, marking the 50th anniversary of the Mustang’s debut and amid unprecedented global demand, Ford unveiled the sixth-generation model after an intensive development effort. This new iteration featured more aggressive styling and introduced 4-wheel independent suspension for the first time in the car’s lineage. Among many variants in the lineup, it is the Mustang GT that captures the hearts of true enthusiasts, thanks to its iconic V-8 powerplant.
car2138.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

car2139.desc: The RC F was unveiled by Lexus at the 2014 Detroit Auto Show. At its heart lay a refined version of the 5.0-liter V-8 from the IS F, producing 449.7 HP and 383.3 ft-lb of torque—an increase of 32.5 HP and 10.8 ft-lb more than the original engine. Paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission featuring paddle shifters, the RC F delivered both power and precision. Excluding the LFA, it stood as the most sports-focused model ever introduced in the Lexus lineup.
car2139.hero: Even beginners can experience dynamic driving performance with a range of electronic aids.

car2141.desc: Unveiled in 2012, the seventh-generation Golf was built on a new platform that introduced a host of advancements. Handling was notably enhanced through the use of XDS—an electronically controlled differential lock—alongside DCC adaptive chassis control and progressive steering. These technologies improved stability and allowed for much higher cornering speeds.
car2141.hero: The GTI version of the 7th-generation Golf ups its handling performance.

car2142.desc: This Vision Gran Turismo concept offered a glimpse into Nissan’s not-too-distant future, brought to life through a collaboration between a youthful team of British designers and Japanese engineers. Its powertrain fuses a twin-turbo V-6 with three electric motors, forming a high-performance hybrid FR-4WD system. With active suspension maximizing its aerodynamic potential, the car remains poised to deliver its full performance the instant the driver calls upon it.
car2142.hero: A look into the future of performance-minded touring cars.

car2143.desc: In 2015, the production Audi R8 underwent a full model change, and with it came the debut of the updated R8 LMS, built to FIA GT3 specifications. This new generation brought significant advancements in both safety and aerodynamics, while the transmission and traction control systems were replaced with newly developed, race-focused components. Mere moments after its unveiling, the R8 LMS proved its capabilities by taking overall victory in its debut outing at the Nürburgring 24 Hours.
car2143.hero: This updated version of a champion race car won the Nürburgring 24 Hour Race immediately after its debut.

car2144.desc: In the fall of 2015, at the Tokyo Motor Show, Toyota unveiled the S-FR lightweight sports car, conceived with the philosophy of delivering “perfect control in an entry model, allowing drivers to fully enjoy the car through everyday engagement." The design captured the spirit of the classic Toyota Sports 800, reimagined with a contemporary sensibility to suit modern tastes.
car2144.hero: Toyota's exciting concept vehicle that carries on the lightweight sports-car torch established by the Sport 800.

car2145.desc: Since its debut in 1998, the Focus ST—the performance model in the Focus lineup—has remained a favorite among driving enthusiasts. The “ST” designation stands for “Sports Technology." In its third generation, the ST adopted a smaller engine than its predecessor, yet output was increased by 24.7 HP, bringing the total to 246.5 HP. Aimed squarely at purists, it retained a 6-speed manual transmission, a rare offering in a market increasingly dominated by two-pedal alternatives.
car2145.hero: Ford's Sport Technology was on full display in this late-model, compact performance car.

car2146.desc: Introduced in 2012, this sports car was created as a spiritual successor to the legendary E-type, which ended production in 1975. Initially offered only as a convertible, a coupe version was added just over a year later. This particular model is the high-performance F-type R Coupé, unveiled alongside the hardtop variant. Powered by a supercharged 5.0-liter V-8 producing 542.4 HP, it could accelerate from zero to 62.1 mph in just 4.2 seconds, with an electronically limited top speed of 186.4 mph.
car2146.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

car2147.desc: The Veneno was a special limited-edition model created to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Lamborghini’s founding. Only three units were ever sold to the public. Based on the Aventador and sharing its chassis and powertrain, the Veneno featured an uprated engine producing 739.6 HP, while weight was reduced through enhancements such as a carbon-fiber monocoque. As a result, the Veneno was 276 lbs lighter than the Aventador, with a total weight of just 3197 lbs.
car2147.hero: Lamborghini celebrated its 50th anniversary with this extremely limited-production super car.

car2148.desc: The fourth-generation ND Roadster made its global debut in April 2014 at the New York Auto Show. Its compact dimensions, combined with a wide, low stance and elegantly sculpted curves, garnered widespread acclaim when the final design was revealed in September of the same year. Pre-orders commenced in March 2015. The entry-level S grade featured pared-down equipment, and at just 2183 lbs, it stood as the only variant with a curb weight under one ton.
car2148.hero: The MX-5 Miata returns to its roots with a lightweight 2183 lbs body and dashing looks.

car2149.desc: The AMG GT was a supercar introduced in 2014 by Mercedes-Benz. Beneath its signature long-nose design sat a rigid aluminum space frame, housing the M178 3982 cc twin-turbo V-8 engine. The high-performance "S" variant pushed output to 502 HP, pairing that power with stiffer suspension and wider tires.
car2149.hero: With a 192.6 mph top speed, this Mercedes-Benz is a race car in street-car clothes.

car2150.desc: Limited to just 1,000 units, this was the final edition of the Lancer Evolution X, although the X itself was omitted from the body, subtly suggesting its role as the last of the legendary line. Based on the 5-speed manual GSR model, it featured an upgraded engine producing 308.7 HP and 311.0 ft-lb of torque, equipped with sodium-filled exhaust valve stems for improved durability. It also came standard with the "high-performance package," which included Bilstein dampers and Eibach springs.
car2150.hero: An icon bodes farewell with a special Final Edition model.

car2152.desc: The car shown here represents the most extreme performance version of the third-generation Charger, which originally launched in 2005. Developed by SRT, Chrysler’s high-performance division, the Charger SRT Hellcat adds a supercharger to the 6.2-liter Hemi V-8, resulting in 707.1 HP and 585.9 ft-lb of torque. Capable of accelerating from zero to 60 mph in just 3.7 seconds and reaching a top speed of 203.8 mph, it briefly held the title of the world’s fastest 4-door sedan.
car2152.hero: Dodge pulls no punches with the Charger SRT Hellcat, one of the most potent sedans in the world.

car2153.desc: Introduced in the autumn of 2013, the Subaru WRX compact sedan emerged as a standalone model, separating itself from the Impreza lineup. Built on a platform closely related to that of the Levorg, the WRX featured significant structural reinforcements. The high-performance STI edition took things further, offering enhanced dynamics with newly developed suspension and a refined version of the EJ20 engine, delivering 303.7 HP and 311.0 ft-lb of torque.
car2153.hero: The WRX STI continues its tradition of delivering potent 4WD performance.

car2154.desc: The Toyota 86 represents Toyota’s take on the compact, front-engine/rear-wheel-drive sports car co-developed with Subaru. Its front-mid-engine-mounted, naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter DOHC boxer engine produced 197.2 HP and 144.7 ft-lb of torque. Many components were freshly designed specifically for this model, resulting in precise, responsive handling that made the driver feel truly connected to the car. It was a next-generation lightweight sports car, created with driving enthusiasts at its core.
car2154.hero: The rebirth of the AE86, Toyota creates an exciting 21st-century version of the ideal sports car.

car2155.desc: This was the high-performance variant of the fifth-generation Polo, Volkswagen’s standout in the compact car segment. Initially powered by a 1.4-liter engine featuring both a supercharger and turbocharger, the 2014 update saw a switch to a 1.8-liter turbocharged unit, delivering 189.3 HP along with improved fuel efficiency. With performance worthy of the GTI badge, it stood as a strong contender among B-segment hot hatches.
car2155.hero: The 'hot' version of the 5th generation Polo uses an advanced engine setup.

car2156.desc: The "Honda Project 2&4 powered by RC213V" was the result of a collaboration between Honda’s design team and Gran Turismo. It combined the 212 HP engine from the Honda RC213V-S with an ultra-lightweight 893 lbs body, creating a unique form of mobility that offered the open-air freedom and agility of a motorcycle, combined with the handling precision and lateral G-forces of a 4-wheeled vehicle.
car2156.hero: A new species with the openness of a motorcycle and the handling of an automobile.

car2157.desc: This Gran Turismo Original takes Aston Martin’s mid-range Vantage sports car and reimagines it to comply with Gr.4 race regulations. Its spirited V-8 engine delivers strong straight-line performance, while the car’s near-perfect weight distribution contributes to superb cornering dynamics, resulting in a highly capable racing machine.
car2157.hero: Aston Martin's Porsche 911 fighter: The new Vantage.

car2158.desc: The 458 Italia GT3 was a regulation-compliant race version of the road-going 458. It featured a lower front bumper functioning as an air dam and a prominent rear wing. Although the engine remained the same, a restrictor limited output to 542.4 HP. Making its debut in 2011, it immediately made its mark by winning the FIA GT3 European Championship.
car2158.hero: This car, which generates more downforce than any Ferrari before it, won the FIA-GT European Championship title.

car2159.desc: The Mustang Gr.3 is a Gran Turismo Original creation, transforming Ford’s legendary Mustang coupe into a machine built to meet Gr.3 race regulations. Its fenders have been dramatically widened to accommodate broader tires, while large rear air outlets were integrated to efficiently channel airflow. This modern muscle car excels through the stability offered by its long wheelbase and boasts an exceptional top speed that’s hard to match.
car2159.hero: The sixth-generation Mustang marked the model’s 50th anniversary and was sold in 120 countries around the world.

car216.desc: Masterminded by Gordon Murray, this car is the racing evolution of the high-performance road-going McLaren F1. After its debut in 1995, the car underwent continuous development, culminating in the introduction of this aerodynamically enhanced Long Tail version in 1997. The F1 GTR enjoyed a long racing career, remaining at the forefront of GT competition under privateer teams all the way through to 2003.
car216.hero: This F1 GTR race car took many racing titles around the world, including the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
car216.nameLong: BMW McLaren F1 GTR Race Car '97

car2160.desc: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been modified to meet Gr.3 regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. With a wheelbase exceeding 110.2 inches, it delivers excellent stability and strong downforce thanks to its expansive floor surface. The naturally-aspirated V-6 produces more than 493.1 HP, offering impressive performance without forced induction. It was a well-balanced machine, capable of excelling through both corners and straights.
car2160.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

car2161.desc: Nissan’s "multi-performance" R35 GT-R has been adapted for Gr.4 competition in this Gran Turismo Original. Its 4-wheel-drive system delivered exceptional handling stability, while endurance racing features—such as integrated fog lamps—make it a well-rounded machine built for long-distance performance.
car2161.hero: Despite a touch of maturity, the new GT-R still possessed the heart of a monster.

car2162.desc: This was one of Ferrari’s flagship special models—continuing the legacy of the F40, F50, and Enzo Ferrari. It was built using the same materials and techniques found in Ferrari’s Formula 1 program, with a carbon monocoque chassis and a specially tuned version of the 6.3-liter V-12 engine from the F12berlinetta, producing 788 HP, enhanced further by the HY-KERS hybrid system. Performance was nothing short of astounding: 0–62.1 mph in under 3 seconds, 0–124.3 mph in under 7 seconds, and a top speed exceeding 217.5 mph.
car2162.hero: Ferrari’s first hybrid car, built with the same materials and processes as an F1 racing machine.

car2163.desc: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been adapted to meet Gr.4 regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. Although it appears externally as a touring car, features like its paddle-shift transmission brought it closer in spirit to a Gr.3 machine. In the real world, this car earned a strong reputation in the drifting scene, and this Gr.4 version proves just as capable for racing as it was for sliding sideways.
car2163.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

car2164.desc: The Mustang Gr.4 is a Gran Turismo Original model that reimagines Ford’s iconic Mustang coupe to comply with Gr.4 race regulations. Built upon the inherently stable platform of the production model, this touring car is an ideal choice for newcomers. Visually, it commands attention with the timeless appeal of classic Ford racing stripes adorning its exterior.
car2164.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

car2166.desc: The 4C Gr.4 is a Gran Turismo original model based on Alfa Romeo's new-generation mid-engine sports car, the 4C, modified to meet Gr.4 standards. Essentially a refined version of the production model, it may have lacked outright power, but its compact footprint and sharp handling gives it a distinct edge on technical circuits.
car2166.hero: The launch edition of the 4C, limited to 1000 units, sold out almost immediately after going on sale.

car2167.desc: In 2016, the Nissan GT-R underwent its most significant facelift since its 2007 debut. The updated exterior achieved a refined balance of aerodynamics, downforce, and cooling efficiency. Its twin-turbo 3.8-liter V-6 engine, now producing 565.1 HP, was paired with an improved 6-speed dual-clutch transmission, delivering smoother acceleration and sharper cornering performance. These deeper, more focused refinements embodied the essence of Japanese sports car engineering.
car2167.hero: Despite a touch of maturity, the new GT-R still possessed the heart of a monster.

car2169.desc: The third-generation TT made its debut in 2014. While it retained the core design philosophy of its predecessors, it adopted a more aggressive look, highlighted by a larger single-frame grille and headlights inspired by the R8. At the top of the range sat the TTS, the flagship sports variant, equipped with a 2.0 TFSI turbocharged 4-cylinder engine tuned to produce 309.7 HP and 274.9 ft-lb of torque in the German domestic model. Paired with a 6-speed manual transmission and Audi’s quattro all-wheel-drive system, it delivered a truly exhilarating driving experience.
car2169.hero: With more power, the sporty version of the third-gen TT took a good thing and made it even better.

car2170.desc: This high-performance model joined the third-generation A-Class lineup one year after the platform's debut. Powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine tuned by AMG, it delivered 355 HP and 325.5 ft-lb of torque. It accelerated from zero to 62.1 mph in 4.6 seconds and reached its electronically limited top speed of 155.3 mph. To manage its power, the car employed a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission routed through a 4-wheel-drive system. Both the braking system and suspension were also upgraded.
car2170.hero: The ultimate hot hatch based on the third-generation A Class.

car2171.desc: The Huracán was unveiled in 2014 as the replacement for the Gallardo. Its construction shifted from an aluminum space frame to a hybrid structure of aluminum and carbon fiber, resulting in a 50 percent increase in rigidity and a 10 percent reduction in weight. Positioned amidships, the 5.2-liter V-10 engine delivered 601.6 HP and 412.3 ft-lb of torque. Power was routed through a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission and sent to the pavement via the Haldex 5 all-wheel-drive system.
car2171.hero: With aesthetics inspired by the Gallardo, this AWD supercar's powerful and lightweight nature makes it ideal for the race track.

car2172.desc: This premium compact was introduced in 2009. Although it shared its platform with the Citroën C3, it carried the DS badge and stood out with distinctive styling and a notably higher level of quality. The DS 3 Racing was a special edition released to commemorate the brand’s entry into the WRC in 2011. Developed by Citroën Racing, it featured a boost in engine output along with chassis enhancements.
car2172.hero: A performance car that boasted exceptional quality and a high level of uniqueness.

car2173.desc: The third-generation Atenza also came equipped with Mazda’s SKYACTIV-D diesel engine. Nicknamed XD (cross-d), it was offered in three trims, with the L package as the highest specification. Thanks to features like idle-stop and i-ELOOP regenerative braking, SKYACTIV-D models achieved fuel economy figures of 52.7 MPG under Japan’s JC08 test cycle.
car2173.hero: The third-generation Mazda 6 features a flowing body style and SKYACTIV technology.
car2173.nameLong: Mazda Atenza Sedan XD L Package '15

car2174.desc: The McLaren 650S was introduced in 2014. Its twin-turbo 3.8-liter V-8, inherited from earlier models, was tuned to produce 641 HP and 499.1 ft-lb of torque to match its name. Paired with a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission for seamless gear changes, it accelerated from zero to 62.1 mph in 3.0 seconds, covered 1312.3 ft in 10.5, and reached a top speed of 206.9 mph.
car2174.hero: The 650S supercar came loaded with F1 technology.

car2175.desc: The "Baby Aston" was developed with the goal of delivering top-tier performance. This front-engine/rear-wheel-drive sports car first appeared in 2005, powered by a 4.3-liter V-8 engine. In 2008, displacement was increased to 4.7 liters, resulting in improved performance across the board. The Vantage S was a special high-performance variant introduced in 2011. In addition to its uprated engine, it featured a stiffer suspension setup and a quicker steering ratio, delivering a sharper driving experience.
car2175.hero: Aston Martin's Porsche 911 fighter: The new Vantage.

car2176.desc: First capturing attention with its debut as a concept at the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show, the Peugeot RCZ transitioned to production in 2010 with remarkably few changes from its original design. In 2015, the lineup was enhanced with the introduction of the GT Line model, which brought a new front grille, dual exhaust outlets, 19-inch alloy wheels, and a red-stitched black leather interior.
car2176.hero: A unique car with a double-bubble rear roof.

car2177.desc: Unveiled in January 2015, the Huracán GT3 was a dedicated racing version of the Huracán, built to FIA GT3 specifications. While it retained the aluminum and carbon fiber hybrid construction of the road car, the body width was increased. Numerous aerodynamic enhancements were added, giving it a more aggressive and purposeful appearance.
car2177.hero: Dallara took the best elements of the Huracán and created a radical competition GT3 machine.

car2178.desc: Unveiled at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show, the S-FR Racing Concept was a track-focused evolution of Toyota’s S-FR. Fender width was extended by 0.8 inches on each side, while a prominent air outlet was integrated into the hood. A large rear wing and aggressive aerodynamic elements transformed the once-playful S-FR Concept into a car exuding the aura of a GT racer.
car2178.hero: The racing version of the attention-getting S-FR concept car.

car2179.desc: A version of the Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo concept car has been developed in collaboration with Gran Turismo and adapted to meet Gr.1 regulations. Thanks to its wide track and 4-wheel-drive system, the base platform delivers excellent stability, resulting in a surprisingly approachable race car.
car2179.hero: A dream machine made to be the pinnacle of race cars and a true Bugatti.

car2180.desc: Originally created through a collaboration between Hyundai and Gran Turismo, the N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo has been reworked to meet Gr.1 regulations in this original model. In accordance with Gr.1 rules, the variable rear wing is fixed in place. The 4-wheel-drive system remains unchanged, giving the car exceptional grip and allowing it to handle as if it were glued to the tarmac.
car2180.hero: This extreme car embodies the passion and future of Hyundai's "N" brand.

car2181.desc: This Gr.1-spec evolution of the LM55 Vision Gran Turismo represents Mazda’s vision of a modern rotary-powered prototype. It delivers the razor-sharp cornering Mazda is known for, enhanced by the exceptional grip of a 4-wheel-drive system. With the ability to dart through corners and surge down straights, it stands as a true modern embodiment of the legendary "rotary rocket."
car2181.hero: A fusion of speed and elegance, born from the spirit of an unrelenting challenger.

car2182.desc: The 650S GT3 was developed as a full FIA-GT3 compliant race car, derived directly from the production McLaren 650S. While it retained the same twin-turbo 3.8-liter V-8, power output was reduced to 493.1 HP to comply with GT3 regulations, similar to the MP4-12C GT3. Additional upgrades included extensive endurance-focused refinements throughout the car. The 650S GT3 earned significant victories in 2015, winning at GT Asia and later claiming top honors at the 2016 Bathurst 12 Hour.
car2182.hero: The GT3 successor to the remarkable MP4-12C race car.

car2183.desc: This Gran Turismo Original took the final front-engine Corvette—the C7—and transformed it to meet Gr.3 regulations. Its exterior has been purpose-built for endurance racing, featuring prominent fog lamps and a distinctively shaped rear wing. Underneath, the raw acceleration of the large-displacement V-8 combined with the sharp, balanced handling of a front-mid-engine layout showcases what a front-engine/rear-drive race car should be.
car2183.hero: The daunting Stingray moniker was resurrected with the seventh-generation Chevrolet Corvette.

car2184.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Jaguar’s new-generation F-type coupe has been reimagined to comply with Gr.3 regulations. This race machine preserves the elegance of the production model’s design, while adopting a more aggressive stance with wide fenders. A key highlight is the swan-neck rear wing, extending from the tail lights, delivering both structural rigidity and increased downforce.
car2184.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

car2185.desc: This Gran Turismo Original reimagines Mitsubishi’s high-performance Lancer Evolution Final Edition as a machine built to meet Gr.3 racing regulations. Stripped of all non-essential elements, the design focuses purely on function. Slits on the front fenders channel turbulent air out of the wheel wells, while an array of winglets inside the fenders carefully manage airflow across the entire body.
car2185.hero: Saying goodbye to the Evo was made easier by the awesome prowess of the "Final Edition" model.
car2185.nameLong: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution Final Edition Gr.3

car2186.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Subaru’s high-performance WRX sedan has been modified to meet Gr.3 racing regulations. To reduce the frontal cross-sectional area, the lower chassis has been trimmed and the overall ride height lowered as much as possible. Equipped with a diffuser-style front splitter and a two-level rear wing, this 4-door sedan generates more downforce than many coupes.
car2186.hero: The WRX STI continues its tradition of delivering potent 4WD performance.

car2187.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a Gr.3 specification version of Toyota’s next-generation racing concept, the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo. The base FT-1 has been outfitted with wide fenders, a prominent rear wing, and a front splitter, transforming it into a cutting-edge race car.
car2187.hero: The FT-1 design concept transformed into a pure race car.

car2188.desc: Based on Renault Sport’s purpose-built one-make racer, the R.S.01, the Renault Sport R.S.01 GT3 was developed to compete in FIA GT championships. To comply with FIA GT3 regulations, the car underwent significant modifications. The power output was restricted, and the brake materials were replaced. Also, 110 lbs of ballast was added, and the ground effect aerodynamics were completely reengineered
car2188.hero: Renault's special GT3 machine with Nismo power.

car2190.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this Gr.3-spec version of the GT by Citroën is born from a unique collaboration between Gran Turismo and Citroën. Unlike the stock model, its aggressive exterior—reminiscent of a battle-ready machine—leaves a striking impression. Fitted with multiple aerodynamic winglets across the body, it delivers exceptional downforce.
car2190.hero: This concept car for the virtual world was developed in collaboration with Citroën.

car2192.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a Gr.3 specification version of the GTI Vision Gran Turismo, a concept born from the collaboration between Volkswagen and Gran Turismo. Significant aerodynamic enhancements were made, including an extended front splitter and an enlarged rear wing.
car2192.hero: This supercar with the GTI's DNA possesses race car-like acceleration.

car24.desc: The 180SX arrived in March 1989 as the liftback variant of the S13 Silvia. Initially set to end production alongside the S13, it was given new life as demand continued abroad. The U.S.-market 240SX, powered by a 2.4-liter engine, remained popular, prompting Nissan to decouple the 180SX from the Silvia lineage. The 180SX became a favorite among enthusiasts who personalized it to suit their tastes and style.
car24.hero: This front-engine/rear-wheel-drive specialty car was given a different character to its sister car, the Silvia.

car293.desc: A high-performance variant of the NSX was introduced in November 1992. Weight was reduced by 265 lbs through the elimination of luxury amenities and the use of lighter functional components. Each engine was carefully balanced to deliver a refined and exhilarating experience at high rpm. It remains a legendary model, one whose significance in the evolution of the NSX cannot be overstated.
car293.hero: The first of the Honda Type R series, only 500 cars of this rare model were produced.

car296.desc: Mazda’s 787B completed the 1991 24 Hours of Le Mans without a single mechanical issue, making history as the first Japanese manufacturer to secure an overall win at the event. Mazda, which had entered Le Mans with rotary engines beginning in 1974, developed the 787 as its final bid for rotary-powered victory, before regulations would turn against such powertrains. Although the effort fell short at the 1990 race, the 787 underwent extensive revisions and emerged as the 787B.
car296.hero: The legendary Mazda 787B was the first Japanese-manufactured race car to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

car301.desc: In August 1996, the second-generation Lancer was introduced, bringing with it the Lancer Evolution IV. The 4G63 engine was rotated 180 degrees compared to previous models and delivered 276.1 HP with a peak torque of 260.4 ft-lb. A major advancement came with the rear differential, where the traditional mechanical LSD was replaced by an electronically controlled AYC (Active Yaw Control) system—greatly enhancing handling precision.
car301.hero: The 4th-gen Evo's handling got a boost from electronic Active Yaw Control and power now up to 276.1 HP.

car31.desc: The original Ford Mustang was an unprecedented success upon its debut as a compact sports coupe. In response, Chevrolet set out to surpass Ford’s achievement, unveiling the Camaro as a direct competitor in the autumn of 1966. The Z28 represented the Camaro at its performance peak. This special variant featured a larger-displacement engine and an enhanced chassis, developed to meet the regulations of the Trans-Am production-based race category.
car31.hero: The Z28 is one of the most popular muscle cars ever, thanks to its good looks and high performance.

car315.desc: Shelby developed the Cobra 427 with the goal of winning the FIA Speed World Challenge, where the team was actively competing at the time. The car was powered by a formidable 7.0-liter 427 “Side Oiler” V-8—a purpose-built race engine originally designed for stock car competition. To handle its impressive 493.1 HP output, the Cobra 427 replaced its signature side-mounted leaf springs with a modern double wishbone suspension, greatly enhancing its handling and stability.
car315.hero: Lightweight and powerful, the Cobra is an American sports car icon.

car3183.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a Gr.3-spec version of the PEUGEOT Vision Gran Turismo, developed through a collaboration between Peugeot and Gran Turismo. To enhance aerodynamic performance, the front splitter and rear diffuser have been enlarged, while a swan-neck rear wing was added.
car3183.hero: Experience pure steering response in a car that generates powerful downforces directly from its body panels.

car3185.desc: The 4C Gr.3 is a Gran Turismo original model based on Alfa Romeo's new-generation mid-engine sports car, the 4C, modified to meet Gr.3 standards. To boost stability and aerodynamics, its wheelbase has been lengthened by 4.3 inches and its revised front overhang grew 1.2 inches. The Gr.4 4C is essentially a refined, tuned variant of the base model. Although less powerful, it exploited its light weight and small footprint to remain competitive in corners.
car3185.hero: The launch edition of the 4C, limited to 1000 units, sold out almost immediately after going on sale.

car3187.desc: This was a single-seater concept created by the famed French marque Alpine, developed specifically for Gran Turismo players. Its design reflected Alpine’s core philosophy of “speed and excitement, embodied in style,” while simultaneously paying tribute to the brand’s iconic past. The result was a groundbreaking machine that blended road and track, and bridged the divide between the virtual and the real.
car3187.hero: A legendary brand's glimpse of the ultimate future sports car.

car3188.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this Gr.1-spec version of the Dodge SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo was the result of a collaboration between Gran Turismo and Dodge. To ensure that its 700 horsepower-plus was effectively translated to the ground, the car was outfitted with aerodynamic enhancements. These included an extended front splitter, a prominent rear wing, and four canards.
car3188.hero: A mid-engine rear-wheel drive version of the Tomahawk for Gr.1 competition.
car3188.nameLong: Dodge SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo (Gr.1)

car3192.desc: The SLS supercar paid tribute to Mercedes-Benz’s storied design heritage. This Gr.4 variant is a Gran Turismo Original. Fitted with a GT3-style roll cage, its long-nose, short-deck proportions echo the legendary 300SL, contributing to impressive cornering stability. Yet it’s not all about handling—the classic V-8 engine delivers formidable straight-line speed that’s equally hard to overlook.
car3192.hero: With the SLS AMG, Mercedes-Benz recreates the 300 SL for the modern era.

car3209.desc: This Gran Turismo Original safety car is based on BMW’s latest-generation high-performance M4 coupe. Building on the M Performance Edition, it features a range of specially designed components, including a front lip spoiler, hood pins, grille garnishes, a rear spoiler, and a rear diffuser.
car3209.hero: A special safety-car version of the BMW M4.

car3210.desc: The AMG GT was a supercar introduced in 2014 by Mercedes-Benz. Beneath its signature long-nose design sat a rigid aluminum space frame, housing the M178 3982 cc twin-turbo V-8 engine. The high-performance "S" variant pushed output to 502 HP. This particular model was modified as a Safety Car.
car3210.hero: With a 192.6 mph top speed, this Mercedes-Benz is a race car in street-car clothes.

car3214.desc: The Civic Type R has thrilled driving enthusiasts worldwide since its debut in 1997. A new model was developed on the ninth-generation European-market 5-door hatchback, undergoing extensive wind tunnel and circuit testing in the pursuit of pure performance. It set a benchmark at the Nürburgring Nordschleife with a lap time of 7 minutes and 50.63 seconds, establishing a new record for front-wheel-drive production cars.
car3214.hero: One of the world's most beloved pocket rockets comes back with a vengeance.

car3215.desc: Peugeot’s 208 GTi continued the tradition, based on the popular 208 compact hatch. Smaller than its predecessor, the 207, it shed more than 220 lbs thanks to a redesigned structure and materials. Its 142.9 mph top speed and 0–62.1 mph acceleration time of 6.8 seconds placed it among the top-tier hot hatches.
car3215.hero: An exciting hot hatch with a distinctive French character.

car3216.desc: In the summer of 2014, Renault Sport unveiled the R.S.01 as its new contender for one-make racing, succeeding the Mégane Trophy. Measuring 164.2 inches in length and 78.7 inches in width, the R.S.01 boasted a lightweight body at just 2425 lbs. Beneath its sculpted exterior was a potent twin-turbo V-6 engine producing 542.4 HP. Every detail of the car—from its advanced aerodynamics to its efficient cooling systems—reflects Renault Sport’s deep expertise, making it an impressive race machine in every sense.
car3216.hero: A French race car with a Japanese heart.

car3217.desc: The sixth-generation Camaro made its debut in 2015. While the exterior continued the retro-modern theme of its predecessor, the underlying structure featured an entirely new design. Built on the new Alpha platform, the car employed aluminum extensively, resulting in 28 percent more rigidity and a weight reduction of 198 lbs. The SS performance model came equipped with a 6.2-liter V-8 engine, and included 20-inch wheels and Brembo brakes as standard.
car3217.hero: The sports grade model of the 6th generation Camaro with the 6.2-liter LT1 engine.

car3218.desc: BMW announced its entry into the FIA GT3 category with the M6 GT3, beginning in the 2016 season. At 16.4 ft long and 6.6 ft wide, it presented a noticeably larger footprint compared to its predecessor, the compact Z4 GT3. Gran Turismo series producer Kazunori Yamauchi competed in the Nürburgring 24 Hours behind the wheel of the Walkenhorst Motorsport M6 GT3, finishing the race and placing 22nd overall.
car3218.hero: The car driven by Kazunori Yamauchi in the 2016 24 Hours of Nürburgring.

car3219.desc: Making its official debut 25 years after the original, the second-generation NSX emerged as a true supercar, equipped with an advanced electric all-wheel-drive system called the Sports Hybrid SH-AWD, which employed independent electric motors on the front wheels. By enhancing both acceleration and deceleration, it enabled torque vectoring that provided exceptional stability through corners across the entire speed range.
car3219.hero: Acura's popular exotic sports car returns after a 10-year hiatus.

car3220.desc: The Clio R.S. 220 EDC Trophy is a high-performance variant of the fourth-generation Clio, developed by Renault Sport. This model, known as the R.S. Vision, introduced a distinctive new front bumper design inspired by the pattern of a checkered flag. It also featured updated LED headlights and taillights, along with various other design enhancements throughout.
car3220.hero: This super fast Clio set the compact hatch lap record at the Nürburgring.
car3220.nameLong: Renault Sport Clio R.S. 220 EDC Trophy '15

car3221.desc: This car succeeded the Z4 GT3, which had been BMW’s flagship GT3 racer since 2010. In stark contrast to the compact Z4, it featured a commanding presence, measuring nearly 16.4 ft long and more than 6.6 ft wide. Under the hood, a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V-8 delivered 576.9 HP in its stock configuration. Built primarily from carbon fiber, the car also featured a completely redesigned frame and suspension, setting it far apart from the production M6.
car3221.hero: A powerful GT3 race machine with a 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8.

car3222.desc: Available exclusively through online orders beginning in January 2016, the 86 GRMN was a fully tuned machine crafted by Toyota, based on its beloved 86 sports car. Beyond structural enhancements, its center of gravity was further lowered through the extensive use of lightweight materials. A host of additional refinements were made—not only was power output increased, but the car also received a newly developed close-ratio 6-speed manual transmission, upgraded brakes, and staggered tire sizing between the front and rear.
car3222.hero: The "Nürburgring Meister" in the form of the Toyota 86.

car3223.desc: When the third-generation Viper appeared in 2012, it was accompanied by the announcement of a racing variant—the GTS-R. From that foundation, the GT3-R was developed as a customer-focused race machine for private teams. Created through a collaboration between SRT, Chrysler’s high-performance division, and Riley Technologies, it featured significant weight reduction and a host of aerodynamic upgrades. It quickly demonstrated its competitiveness, proving its racing potential in GT events across America and around the world.
car3223.hero: A machine for private racers, carrying on the bloodline of the GTS-R.

car3224.desc: The AMG GT3 was Mercedes-Benz’s dedicated GT3 race car. It was introduced in 2016 and designed for global GT3 category competition. It quickly proved its worth by securing a remarkable 1-2-3-4 finish in its debut race at the Nürburgring 24 Hours. One of its most successful campaigns came through HTP Motorsport, a top contender in the Blancpain GT Series.
car3224.hero: This race car dominated the 24 Hours of Nürburgring in its very first outing.

car3225.desc: This Gran Turismo Original transformed the R35 GT-R supercar into a dedicated safety car. Equipped with roof-mounted LED patrol lights and additional light arrays on the front and rear bumpers, it offered significantly enhanced visibility. The center console was also fitted with exclusive switches unique to its safety car role.
car3225.hero: This Nissan GT-R, converted into a safety car, was made to patrol the race track.

car3227.desc: The LC500 is a luxury sports coupe that made its debut at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show. While its design featured sleek, flowing lines, the front and rear overhangs were shortened to accommodate a front mid-engine layout with 2+2 seating. A mix of lightweight materials was used throughout the body, achieving a balance of reduced weight and high structural rigidity.
car3227.hero: This stylish sports coupe attracted plenty of attention with its low nose and short overhang design.

car3228.desc: The RC F GT3 is a GT3-spec race car developed from the Lexus RC F, created as a prototype prior to official homologation to evaluate and refine its performance. In its early testing phase, the car claimed victory in Round 9 of the VLN (Nürburgring Endurance Series). At the time, it competed in raw carbon-fiber bodywork, but the version shown here is adorned in the distinctive Emil Frey Racing livery.
car3228.hero: This highly refined Lexus RC F coupe competed in the 2016 VLN as a GT3 race car.

car3229.desc: The Mustang Gr.B was a Gran Turismo Original creation, reimagining Ford’s legendary Mustang coupe to comply with Gr.B rally regulations. Its livery draws inspiration from the factory colors of the Ford GT race program. Although it may have seemed an unlikely candidate at first glance, the car echoes Ford’s rich rallying heritage, embodied by icons like the Escort and RS200, making the concept feel surprisingly authentic.
car3229.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

car3230.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a Gr.B-spec reinterpretation of Mitsubishi’s high-performance sedan, the Lancer Evolution Final Edition. Its white, silver, and red livery pays tribute to the iconic rally machines of Mitsubishi’s storied World Rally Championship past. Fitted with Gr.3-style aerodynamic components, it generates substantial downforce that can challenge even today’s WRC contenders.
car3230.hero: An icon bodes farewell with a special Final Edition model.
car3230.nameLong: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution Final Edition Gr.B Rally Car
car3230.nameShort: Lancer Evolution Final Gr.B Rally Car

car3231.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Volkswagen’s sleek Scirocco sports coupe has been reimagined to meet Gr.4 race standards. Its aerodynamic enhancements are subtle—a modest front splitter and a compact rear wing—underscoring a focus on preserving the strengths of the base model. The result is a front-wheel-drive machine with remarkable cornering prowess.
car3231.hero: This attractive coupe possessed the sharp cornering ability of a full-fledged sports car.

car3232.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Subaru’s high-performance WRX sedan has been modified to comply with Gr.B regulations. To enhance downforce and agility, the car’s track width has been significantly widened, while long-stroke suspension was fitted to improve off-road capability. The result is a cutting-edge rally machine.
car3232.hero: The WRX STI continues its tradition of delivering potent 4WD performance.

car3234.desc: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been reengineered to meet Gr.B regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. A 4-wheel-drive conversion has been added, along with design elements inspired by modern rally machines. The front fenders feature smooth, organic curves to maximize downforce, while the wide track, measuring more than 80.7 inches, enhanced maneuverability, complementing the car’s long wheelbase.
car3234.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

car3235.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX sports car has been reengineered to comply with Gr.3 racing regulations. It features a range of aerodynamic enhancements, including a large front splitter with precision cutouts to manage airflow, and a swan-neck rear wing.
car3235.hero: Acura's popular exotic sports car returns after a 10-year hiatus.

car3237.desc: Mazda’s Atenza global sedan has been specifically modified for Gr.3 competition as part of this Gran Turismo Original. The exterior showcases aggressive yet refined aerodynamics shaped by Mazda’s "KODO" design philosophy. To boost structural rigidity, a bulkhead has been added behind the cockpit, along with a rearview camera to enhance visibility.
car3237.hero: This is an original racing version of the Mazda6 for Gr.3 competition.

car3238.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this is a race-prepared version of the RCZ—Peugeot’s elegantly contoured specialty coupe—adapted for Gr.3 regulations. To enhance weight distribution and overall performance, the drivetrain has been reconfigured from its original front-engine/front-wheel-drive setup to a mid-engine/rear-wheel-drive layout. With its extended 102.8 inches wheelbase, the RCZ provides an ideal foundation for transformation into a competitive race machine.
car3238.hero: This is a Gr.3 race version of the stylish Peugeot RCZ compact coupe.

car3239.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX has been reimagined to conform to Gr.B rally regulations. While sporting a rugged rally-cross exterior, it retains the NSX’s signature mid-engine layout, now paired with a 4-wheel-drive system. The original rear-biased weight distribution has been preserved, promising thrilling tail-out dynamics on loose surfaces.
car3239.hero: The NSX was revived with SH-AWD 25 years after the debut of the original model.

car3241.desc: Nissan’s "multi-performance" R35 GT-R has been reimagined for Gr.B competition in this Gran Turismo Original. The most striking exterior changes includes quad fog lamps mounted on the bonnet and large auxiliary lamps flanking the front bumper, perfect for illuminating night rally stages. Its already exceptional 4-wheel-drive system gives the GT-R a distinct advantage in the world of rallying.
car3241.hero: This Gr.B design reimagines the Nissan GT-R as a dedicated off-road race machine.

car3242.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this Gr.B version of the RCZ reimagines Peugeot’s elegantly sculpted specialty coupe. Designed in the spirit of the extreme Pikes Peak hillclimb cars, it features an oversized front spoiler and a towering rear wing. The drivetrain has been completely reengineered, with the engine relocated behind the cockpit and mated to a 4-wheel-drive system.
car3242.hero: This is an original Gr.B rally-tuned version of the Peugeot RCZ compact coupe.

car3245.desc: This Gran Turismo Original reimagines BMW’s new-generation high-performance M4 coupe as a Gr.4-spec machine. Although styled like a touring car, it retains the precise cornering ability and rock-solid stability that define BMW’s performance legacy. Its well-balanced handling and approachable dynamics make it an ideal choice even for novice drivers.
car3245.hero: This Gran Turismo original Gr.4 race car maximizes the performance of the M4.

car3246.desc: Bugatti’s Veyron supercar has been reimagined to meet Gr.4 regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. Although its power output was reduced from that of the standard model to comply with class rules, it can still hold its own against rivals with impressive straight-line speed. Its 4-wheel-drive system also provides a distinct advantage in cornering, offering exceptional stability through turns.
car3246.hero: With a little help from a special key, this remarkable automobile reached speeds of over 233 mph.

car3247.desc: This Gran Turismo Original reimagines the C7—the final front-engine Corvette—to meet Gr.4 regulations. It retains the base car’s predictable cornering behavior, resulting in a confidence-inspiring driving experience. With impressive straight-line speed to match, it allows drivers to stay competitive across every section of the track.
car3247.hero: The daunting Stingray badge returns with the 7th-gen Chevrolet Corvette.

car3248.desc: Designed for competition in the Gr.4 category, this race car is a modified version of the GT by Citroën, originally unveiled at the 2008 Paris Motor Show. The updates were overseen by Takumi Yamamoto, the designer behind the original concept. Its exterior features a striking six-color livery and a prominent rear wing. Also, the interior has been revised with a new steering wheel and updated HUD to suit its motorsports focus.
car3248.hero: This concept car for the virtual world was developed in collaboration with Citroën.

car3249.desc: This Gran Turismo Original took Dodge’s high-performance Viper and modified it to comply with Gr.4 regulations. Its exterior features an aggressive front splitter, aerodynamic canards, and a prominent rear wing to generate substantial downforce. The result is a machine that delivered impressive straight-line speed while offering significant potential through the corners as well.
car3249.hero: The third-generation Viper boasted extreme performance that was developed by the SRT division.

car3251.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX sports car has been adapted to meet Gr.4 regulations. This design prioritizes preserving the character of the base car, adding only a subtle front splitter, compact canards, and a rear wing. To enhance structural rigidity, a rear bulkhead has been added, accompanied by a rear camera.
car3251.hero: This second-generation NSX with SH-AWD was modified for Gr.4 competition.

car3252.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Jaguar’s new-generation F-type coupe has been reimagined to comply with Gr.4 regulations. This model features a bold new look, finished in matte gray with the front grille garnishes removed. Despite its styling, the car remains approachable behind the wheel, offering stable cornering and impressive straight-line performance.
car3252.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

car3253.desc: Lamborghini’s entry-level, mid-engine, all-wheel-drive Huracán has been reimagined as a Gr.4-spec machine for this Gran Turismo Original. Its 4-wheel-drive layout provides exceptional stability, while the balanced weight distribution of the mid-engine design delivers sharp cornering, resulting in a well-rounded and highly composed race car.
car3253.hero: With aesthetics inspired by the Gallardo, this AWD supercar's powerful and lightweight nature makes it ideal for the race track.

car3254.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a race-prepared version of the Lexus RC F coupe, specifically modified for Gr.4 competition. Harnessing the immense torque of its large-displacement V-8, the car delivers exceptional straight-line acceleration. Its base color is finished in the signature orange used by Lexus for its exclusive special models.
car3254.hero: This version of the highly refined Lexus RC F production coupe was modified for Gr.4.

car3256.desc: Mazda’s Atenza global sedan has been tailored for Gr.3 use in this Gran Turismo Original. Utilizing a 4-wheel-drive platform, the car delivers exceptional traction. A Gr.3-style front grille and hood vents are fitted to assist the turbocharged 4-cylinder engine in producing its impressive 394.5 HP.
car3256.hero: This is an original racing version of the Mazda6 for Gr.4 competition.

car3257.desc: In the virtual world, the 650S inspired a Gran Turismo Original—the Gr.4 version, modeled on McLaren’s mid-tier supercar. Finished in McLaren’s factory racing color, this virtual machine offered well-balanced handling and predictable behavior. Its cockpit elements, fuel cap, and jack points were faithfully modeled after GT3-level race equipment.
car3257.hero: Here is the Gran Turismo original Gr.4 spec-version of the McLaren 650S super sports car.

car3258.desc: This Gran Turismo Original reinterpreted Mitsubishi’s high-performance Lancer Evolution Final Edition for Gr.4 competition. Building on the Lancer’s proven success in real-world touring car racing, this version carries over the model’s advanced electronically controlled 4-wheel-drive system, delivering exceptional cornering performance and stability on the track.
car3258.hero: This final model closed the curtain on a long and historic WRC career.
car3258.nameLong: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution Final Edition Gr.4

car3259.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this is a Gr.4-spec version of the RCZ, Peugeot’s gracefully styled specialty coupe. Maintaining a front-wheel-drive layout, this model features motorsports-inspired enhancements including a prominent front splitter, a rear wing, and redesigned aerodynamic front fenders.
car3259.hero: This is a Gr.4 race car version of the stylish Peugeot RCZ compact coupe.

car3260.desc: This Gran Turismo Original is a Gr.4-spec version of Renault’s fastest hatchback, the Mégane. Having already proven itself with a blistering Nürburgring lap time, the Mégane's transformation into a race car felt like a natural progression. With outstanding traction and sharp cornering capabilities, it delivers such precise performance that you’ll forget it’s front-wheel drive at all.
car3260.hero: This limited-edition Renault set a lap record at the Nürburgring.

car3261.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Subaru’s high-performance WRX sedan has been modified to meet Gr.4 racing regulations. A front splitter and rear wing have been added to generate additional downforce. The base car’s 4-wheel-drive system is retained, giving it class-leading traction among the Gr.4 field.
car3261.hero: The WRX STI continues its tradition of delivering potent 4WD performance.

car3262.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this version of Toyota’s new sports car, the 86, has been specially modified to comply with Gr.4 racing regulations. While the 86 had already seen action in clubman-level motorsports across the globe, this iteration transforms it into a true race machine, with its power output raised to 364 horsepower. It excels through corners, where its lightweight and compact body can be fully exploited to deliver exceptional handling.
car3262.hero: This is a Gran Turismo original version of the Toyota 86 FR sports car modified for Gr.4.

car3263.desc: The 458 Gr.4 is a Gran Turismo Original entry-level race model in Ferrari’s lineup. While its aero-package was subtle, the base car’s downforce and handling remains intact. Combined with the Ferrari V-8 and 7-speed gearbox, it offers strong performance on the circuit.
car3263.hero: With an astonishing 562.1 HP under the hood, this mid-engine V-8-powered machine drew its inspiration from the F430.

car3264.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, Ford’s Focus global hatchback has been reimagined to meet the demands of Gr.B regulations. To accommodate the changes, air intakes have been added just ahead of the rear fenders, channeling airflow to a rear-mounted radiator. Relocating the radiator to the trunk improved weight distribution, making it one of the most easy-to-drive machines in the Gr.B category.
car3264.hero: The chassis performance of the late third-generation model shines in this rally special.

car3265.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this version of Toyota’s new sports car, the 86, has been specially modified to comply with Gr.B racing regulations. The car has been transformed into a top-class rally machine, with its original rear-wheel-drive layout converted to 4-wheel drive, while aggressive aerodynamic elements such as canards and a two-level rear wing generated substantial downforce.
car3265.hero: This off-road version of Toyota's 86 was modified for Gr.B competition.

car3266.desc: This electric vehicle was unveiled by BMW in 2013. Its distinctive, boxy 4-door body featured small, pillarless rear doors, and weighed just 2634 lbs, thanks to an aluminum alloy chassis paired with a carbon-fiber cabin. The electric motor produced 167.7 HP and 180.8 ft-lb of torque, enabling the car to accelerate from zero to 37.3 mph in 3.7 seconds, and to 62.1 mph in 7.2 seconds. With a top speed exceeding 93.2 mph, it proved it can compete with its internal combustion-powered counterparts.
car3266.hero: BMW’s first mass-produced production vehicle has a sports-car heart.

car3267.desc: The F12berlinetta was introduced in 2012 as Ferrari’s new flagship grand tourer, succeeding the 599 GTB Fiorano. Built around an all-new aluminum space frame and body shell, it featured a front-mid-mounted V-12 engine. With its optimized layout, it accelerated from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.1 seconds and reaching a top speed of 211.3 mph. It also claimed the lap record at Ferrari’s Fiorano test track.
car3267.hero: The flagship model of Ferrari wasn't just fast, it was a technological marvel.

car3268.desc: This high-performance model served as a further evolution of the 991-generation Porsche 911 GT3. Starting with the wide-body shell of the 911 Turbo, Porsche increased front and rear track widths, while also implementing major weight reductions and aerodynamic enhancements. The engine, enlarged to 4.0 liters, produced 493.1 HP and enabled the car to record a Nürburgring Nordschleife lap time of 7 minutes and 20 seconds.
car3268.hero: The ultimate 991, rebuilt from the ground up.

car3295.desc: Released in 2012, the Toyota 86 was a sports car that combined a compact body with a rear-wheel-drive layout. The first minor update came in 2016, enhancing body rigidity and aerodynamics. Models equipped with the 6-speed manual transmission received engine retuning along with upgrades to numerous components, placing greater emphasis on performance rather than appearance. The GT Limited trim represented the highest grade in the 86 lineup. Its interior featured upscale materials such as leather and Alcantara, offering a more premium and mature cabin environment.
car3295.hero: The "classic" Toyota 86 sports car takes on a more mature character.

car3296.desc: A homologation model of the C7 Gr.3, a race-prepped version of the final front-engine Corvette, meets Gr.3 competition standards. Visually, it stands out with a bold design that pushes right up to the 80.7 inches width limit allowed in the category. Despite its broad stance, the car is exceptionally agile, with race-spec suspension allowing for quick and precise cornering, revealing its true identity as a purpose-built performance machine
car3296.hero: The daunting Stingray badge returns with the 7th-gen Chevrolet Corvette.
car3296.nameLong: Chevrolet Corvette C7 Gr.3 Road Car

car3297.desc: In June 2016, a Subaru WRX STI set a new record for 4-wheeled vehicles during a time attack on the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy course. While Subaru had been competing in the event since 2011, the 2016 machine was specially prepared by Britain’s Prodrive, a team renowned for its multiple World Rally Championship titles. Thanks to their expertise, the record was lowered by nearly two minutes, with a final time of 17:35.139 and an average speed of 128.6 mph.
car3297.hero: This celebrated WRX set the lap record on the holy ground of motorcycle racing, the Isle of Man.
car3297.nameLong: Subaru WRX STI Isle of Man Time Attack Car '16

car3298.desc: This racing machine was based on the Audi TT and developed specifically for the Audi Sport TT Cup one-make series. Sections of the body shell were replaced with carbon fiber, and all driver comforts were stripped away, reducing the car’s weight to just 2480 lbs. It was powered by a 305.7 HP 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engine, the same unit found in the standard TTS, but enhanced with a "push to pass" system that temporarily boosted output by an additional 29.6 HP.
car3298.hero: These TTs were produced specifically for the "Audi Sport TT Cup" one-make race.

car3299.desc: The 4C Gr.3 is a homologation version of Alfa Romeo’s 4C mid-engine sports car that was developed to meet Gr.3 standards. The already agile base model has been transformed with a wider body, and the engine's power was boosted from 200 to 450 horsepower.
car3299.hero: This road car version of the Gr.3 4C sold 1000 units as soon as it was released to the public.

car3300.desc: This particular version serves as a homologation model of the Mustang Gr.3—a Gran Turismo Original that reimagines Ford’s legendary coupe to comply with Gr.3 racing regulations. With its roots in motorsport, the car’s performance has been finely tuned, placing particular emphasis on cornering prowess. A true all-rounder, it excels equally in circuit time attacks and controlled drifting alike.
car3300.hero: The sixth-generation Mustang marked the model’s 50th anniversary and was sold in 120 countries around the world.

car3301.desc: A homologation model of the Lancer Evolution Final Edition Gr.B, this version has been originally developed as a rally base car. Thanks to its near-perfect 50:50 weight distribution and extended rear wing, it delivers handling on paved roads that few other 4-wheel-drive vehicles could match.
car3301.hero: This Gr.B rally machine is a highly tuned version of the final Lancer Evolution.
car3301.nameLong: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution Final Edition Gr.B Road Car
car3301.nameShort: Lancer Evolution Final Gr.B Road Car

car3303.desc: This is the homologation model of the RCZ Gr.3, a race-spec version of Peugeot’s gracefully sculpted specialty coupe, adapted for Gr.3 regulations. Transformed into a mid-engine supercar, the design draws inspiration from the 2002 RC concept, one of the earliest visions that eventually gave rise to the RCZ.
car3303.hero: This is a Gr.3 production version of the stylish Peugeot RCZ compact coupe.

car3304.desc: This is the homologation model of the WRX Gr.B, a variant of Subaru’s high-performance WRX sedan engineered to meet Gr.B regulations. Although rooted in rally car design, greater emphasis has been placed on on-road performance, with the addition of a race-inspired front splitter, side skirt winglets, and a rear diffuser.
car3304.hero: This road-going version of the WRX Gr.B was modified to excel on the tarmac.

car3305.desc: The Beetle Gr.3 is a racing variant of Volkswagen’s iconic compact, engineered to comply with Gr.3 regulations. The once-playful road car has been thoroughly reworked into a serious contender, with major changes including a switch from front- to rear-wheel drive and a lowered roofline to reduce frontal area and improve aerodynamics.
car3305.hero: This Gr.3 race version of the Volkswagen Beetle is on an entirely different level to the road-going model.

car3306.desc: This is a Gr.3 homologation model of the Atenza, derived from Mazda’s global market sedan and adapted to comply with Gr.3 racing regulations. Engineered as a true race machine, it has been transformed into a high-performance sedan producing more than 400 horsepower. Its design stands out for considering even the flow of reflections across the bodywork.
car3306.hero: The third-generation Mazda6 featured a curvaceous body style and SkyActiv technology.

car3309.desc: A special circuit-only model limited to 24 units, this car was developed using the knowledge and experience gained from the One-77 project. Its front mid-mounted 7.0-liter V-12 produced 799.8 HP, delivered through a transaxle for optimal weight distribution. Damping, ABS, and traction control could all be fine-tuned to suit the driver’s preferences. Each fortunate owner received full technical support from Aston Martin, along with access to a dedicated circuit driving program.
car3309.hero: With a mere 24 units produced, this hypercar shined on the track and became an instant collector's item.

car3310.desc: A pure racing version was also introduced for the Cayman’s GT4 class. While it retained the same 379.7 HP 3.8-liter flat-6, it was fully optimized for competition, stripped of all comfort features and fitted with components from the 911 GT3 Cup car to maximize track performance.
car3310.hero: The highest performance model of the Cayman series in its naturally aspirated flat 6 generation.

car3311.desc: This race-bred machine carried the spirit of the RSR. And it was developed through an entirely different process than the production 911 road car. Its 4.0-liter naturally-aspirated engine, the first in 911 history to be mid-mounted, delivered 502 HP. At the 2017 Nürburgring 24 Hours, the car delivered a standout performance, holding the top spot for much of the race.
car3311.hero: This 911, the first in history to feature a mid-engine layout, is a full competition spec machine.

car3312.desc: The TS050 - Hybrid was developed for competition in the 2016 World Endurance Championship. It featured motor generator units (MGUs) on both the front and rear axles, paired with a V-6 direct-injection twin-turbocharged engine. The combined output of the engine and electric motors reached 986.2 HP. While the car showed strong potential as a title contender, it ultimately finished 3rd in the drivers’ standings. It also secured 3rd place in the manufacturers’ rankings.
car3312.hero: Toyota's hybrid LMP1 car was developed to dominate the World Endurance Championship.

car3313.desc: This prototype sports car was developed specifically to compete in the World Endurance Championship (WEC) and at Le Mans. It utilized a turbocharged 2.0-liter V-4 as part of a hybrid system that included energy recovery technology, with a total output of 887.6 HP. From 2015 through 2017, it dominated the WEC, capturing both the constructors’ and drivers’ championships in those years.
car3313.hero: The consecutive Le Mans champion & hybrid prototype sports car.

car3314.desc: A Vision Gran Turismo model was developed by Audi Design. Two versions were conceived: one hybrid, the other fully electric. In the hybrid, a turbocharged 3.4-liter V-6 drove the rear wheels, while the front wheels were powered by an electric motor/generator unit, together delivering an impressive 950kW (1274.2 HP). The design of the car paid tribute to the iconic Audi 90 IMSA GTO race machine.
car3314.hero: Taking cues from its IMSA race cars, this Vision Gran Turismo machine represents the future of Audi.

car3315.desc: The McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo was developed as McLaren’s vision of high-performance motoring in 2030 and beyond. Behind the cabin, where the driver lay in a motorcycle-like position, resides a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8. The engine is assisted by high-performance electric motors housed in each of the front wheel pods, bringing the total output to 1134.1 HP.
car3315.hero: Putting the driver before all else, this car is the ultimate realization of the McLaren philosophy.

car3316.desc: The Daihatsu Copen is a compact convertible that delivers a full sports car experience while staying within Japan’s kei-car regulations. The Copen RJ Vision Gran Turismo is based on the second-generation model, which debuted in 2014. While it retains the kei-standard 660 cc engine, boost efficiency has been significantly improved, allowing it to produce 146.9 HP and 149.0 ft-lb of torque. Further weight reduction brings the car down to just 1323 lbs, enabling it to perform on par with larger-displacement sports cars. This bold, aspirational machine carried forward Daihatsu’s fighting spirit.
car3316.hero: A Vision Gran Turismo that represents the potential of kei cars.
car3316.nameLong: DAIHATSU COPEN RJ Vision Gran Turismo

car3332.desc: This Vision Gran Turismo was created as a tribute to Peugeot’s historic triumph at the 1916 Indianapolis 500 Mile Race. Standing at just 3.3 ft tall, the car boasts a low-slung profile, with a gracefully tapered tail reminiscent of the Indy-winning L45 machine. Its powertrain features a hybrid setup, pairing a 1.6-liter turbocharged 4-cylinder engine with two electric motors, delivering a combined output of 493.1 HP and 730 Nm (535.2 ft-lb) of torque.
car3332.hero: This Vision Gran Turismo pays homage to the legendary L45 race machine.
car3332.nameLong: Peugeot L500R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo, 2017

car3333.desc: This is the competition version of the L500R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo. The rev limiter on its 1.6-liter 4-cylinder engine has been raised to 10,000 rpm, boosting peak output to 571 HP. When combined with the 167.7 HP produced by the electric motors, total system output reaches an impressive 739.6 HP. Visually, the car features a prominent front under spoiler and a large rear wing, both added to generate increased downforce.
car3333.hero: This Vision Gran Turismo pays homage to the legendary L45 race machine.
car3333.nameLong: Peugeot L750R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo, 2017

car3334.desc: The Audi R18 was engineered to compete in the 2016 World Endurance Championship (WEC). Its aerodynamics underwent a complete redesign, adopting a F1-inspired narrow nose with integrated wing, while the hybrid system’s regenerative energy capacity was increased from 4MJ to 6MJ. Although Audi secured 2nd place in the Constructors’ Championship, the brand made the difficult decision to withdraw from the WEC at year’s end.
car3334.hero: Audi's history-making LMP1 car dominated the World Endurance Championship in the 2010s.

car3335.desc: A Gran Turismo Original, this Gr.1 machine is based on the McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo, born from a collaboration between McLaren and Gran Turismo. While Gr.1 regulations restrict the use of active aerodynamic elements, the car still delivers exceptional cornering performance thanks to its inherently high-downforce body design and formidable mechanical grip.
car3335.hero: This version of McLaren's future is realized in Gr.1 form with Vision Gran Turismo.

car3336.desc: The F-Series is Ford’s line of full-size pickup trucks, introduced in 1948. Over the decades, it became a staple of American roads and has held the title of the best-selling vehicle in the U.S. for more than 30 years. The F-150 SVT Raptor, developed by Ford’s Special Vehicle Team (SVT), was a purpose-built off-road variant of the F-150, using the same 4-wheel-drive system as its base model, for high-speed desert racing.
car3336.hero: With 411.2 HP on tap, this was one of the most potent pickup trucks ever created, thanks to Ford's Special Vehicle Team.

car3337.desc: The original Alpine A110 proved itself across the globe, performing admirably in rally competition. In 2017, Renault revived the Alpine name to carry the torch forward, revealing the modern Alpine A110. This new version, clad in an aluminum body echoing the original, featured a mid-mounted turbocharged 1.8-liter 4-cylinder engine producing 248.5 HP and 231.5 ft-lb of torque. A special Première Édition was created, with production limited to 1,955 units worldwide.
car3337.hero: This lightweight sports car from the reborn Alpine brand combined elegance with performance.

car3338.desc: It's an imaginative custom hot rod that made its debut at SEMA 2013. Based on a 1967 Chevrolet Nova body, it was outfitted with the supercharged 6.2-liter LS9 engine from the Corvette, paired with racing-grade components across the braking and suspension systems. It took home the prestigious GT Award that year.
car3338.hero: This monster Nova was a 2013 GT Award winner, equipped with the highest quality performance parts available.

car3339.desc: The 2017 Falken Tire / Turn 14 Distribution BRZ was piloted by Formula Drift champion Daijiro Yoshihara. Based on the Rocket Bunny V3 aero kit, the car housed a 7.0-liter turbocharged V-8 that delivered approximately 986.2 HP. A 4-speed transmission and reinforced drivetrain components ensured it could handle the immense power.
car3339.hero: This BRZ competition machine was piloted by Formula Drift champion Daijiro Yoshihara in 2017.

car334.desc: Originally developed for motorsports, the Renault Clio R.S. V6 possessed the 3.0-liter V-6 from the luxury Laguna, producing up to 229.8 HP. In 2002, the updated Phase 2 model raised output to 251.5 HP and introduced changes to the exterior, interior, and tire size.
car334.hero: Built by Tom Walkinshaw Racing, this sporty Lutecia featured a mid-mounted 3.0-liter V6.

car3340.desc: Beginning in 2015, Lexus initiated test competition with a purpose-built race car based on the RC F, using the data and experience gained to refine and evolve the machine. This development culminated in the debut of the RC F GT3 in 2017. Emil Frey Racing, who played a key role in the car's development, campaigned the RC F GT3 in the International GT Open. Its efforts were rewarded with a 3rd-place finish in the team standings.
car3340.hero: Emil Frey Racing was one of the first teams to compete with a GT3 version of the Lexus RC F.

car3341.desc: This was the third model created by De Tomaso. Its sleek body, crafted by Carrozzeria Ghia, was paired with a robust 5.8-liter OHV V-8 sourced from Ford. This striking combination delivered performance on par with its more expensive contemporaries.
car3341.hero: This extremely rare supercar combined vivid Italian design with no-nonsense American power.

car3342.desc: The Gran Turismo F1500T-A was a modern tribute to the mid-1980s era of Formula 1, widely regarded as the golden age of F1 design. Its carbon-fiber chassis measured 166.7 inches in length, 84.5 inches in width, with a wheelbase of 107.0 inches. Power came from a turbocharged 1.5-liter V-6, a hallmark of 1980s F1, producing a staggering 986.2 HP at 11,000 rpm.
car3342.hero: This original formula car adopted the spirit and performance of the mid-1980s Formula 1 race cars.

car3343.desc: Unveiled at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show, the DB11 represented the quintessential Aston Martin. While retaining the brand’s signature silhouette, it distinguished itself from its predecessors with modern design cues. At its heart was a newly developed twin-turbo 5.2-liter V-12 producing 599.6 HP and 513.5 ft-lb of torque, paired with a ZF 8-speed automatic transmission, allowing the car to accelerate from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.9 seconds and reaching a top speed of 206.3 mph.
car3343.hero: Aston Martin's successor to the DB9 featured a new futuristic design theme.

car3344.desc: This coupe was designed for touring car racing and developed by BMW M, based on the E30 3 Series. It featured blistered fenders, front and rear spoilers, and distinctive side skirts, giving it a bold, aggressive appearance. The Sport Evolution was the final version of this M3 generation. Its enlarged 2.5-liter engine produced 234.7 HP and 173.6 ft-lb of torque, making it a formidable force on the circuit.
car3344.hero: This highly modified homologation version of the E30 3 Series served as a small hint of what was to come from BMW.
