The suspension layout mirrored its predecessor’s, utilizing struts up front and a multi-link configuration at the rear. Super HICAS 4-wheel steering system was also offered on a select variant.
car3513.hero: The sixth-generation Silvia emphasized heightened luxury in a wide body format.

car3514.desc: The Citroën DS made its debut at the 1955 Paris Salon, introduced as a groundbreaking front-wheel-drive vehicle that combined a sleek aerodynamic profile with advanced hydropneumatic suspension. It quickly earned the nickname “flying saucer” for its appearance. Development was led by André Lefèbvre, while the striking body was the work of designer Flaminio Bertoni. In 1964, Citroën introduced the upscale Pallas trim, followed by the addition of quad headlights in 1967. The DS 21 Pallas delivered refined performance from its 2.1-liter engine and remained in production for two decades.
car3514.hero: A historic vision of the future from France.

car3518.desc: Released in 2019, the eighth-generation Corvette became the first in the lineup to adopt a mid-engine layout—a major departure from the traditional front-engine design. At its core was the new 6.2-liter LT2 V-8, producing 495.1 HP and 470.1 ft-lb of torque, paired with an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox. Although it left behind the Corvette’s signature long-nose silhouette, the C8 delivered outstanding performance, particularly in GT racing.

car3519.desc: The Porsche 959 was the production evolution of the original Gruppe B prototype, which Porsche had engineered for competition in Group B, the top category of the WRC at the time. It featured an advanced, electronically controlled 4-wheel-drive system that allowed drivers to adjust drivetrain settings to suit various conditions, delivering exceptional stability and ride comfort. Although Group B was disbanded before the car could compete in the WRC, the 959 still achieved remarkable success in other forms of motorsports.
car3519.hero: A four-wheel-drive road car that shines bright in automotive history.

car3520.desc: In an era when Japanese passenger cars were generally capped at 276.1 HP, NISMO defied convention with a fully tuned machine delivering 394.5 HP. At its heart was the RB-X GT2, an enlarged 2.8-liter evolution of the revered RB26, paired with an N1-spec turbocharger. The suspension setup featured Bilstein dampers, reinforced by upgraded stabilizers and bushings. Flared fenders accommodated the wider tires, offering a visual cue to the car’s formidable capabilities.
car3520.hero: Boasting 394.5 HP and an extremely limited production run, this is the ultimate R33 GT-R from Nismo.

car3521.desc: The fourth-generation MAZDA3 made its debut in 2018. A standout addition to the lineup was the mild hybrid M Hybrid, which gained global attention for its SKYACTIV-X engine, utilizing spark-controlled compression ignition. The X Burgundy Selection is a limited-edition variant based on the X grade, featuring the advanced SKYACTIV-X powertrain paired with a rich burgundy interior, offering a mature sense of elegance.
car3521.hero: An elegant fastback with a revolutionary combustion system.

car3522.desc: The 1971 Ford Maverick, winner of the 2018 SEMA “Best of Show,” was crafted by Greening Auto Company into a striking custom build. Its ride height was dropped to the limit for maximum visual impact. The 7.0-liter Windsor V-8 was equipped with twin turbochargers to generate 1199.2 HP, yet it also offered flexibility—its engine control logic could be adjusted for a more relaxed, street-friendly cruise.
car3522.hero: A vicious hot rod with 1200HP and a nostalgic body

car3523.desc: This was a 2019 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters (DTM) machine. In line with the series’ engine downsizing rules, the previous 4.0-liter V-8 was replaced with a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4. Remarkably, the new engine produced more power than its predecessor, while also weighing less, with improved weight distribution. In the 2019 season, Audi’s ace driver René Rast captured the championship title, alongside securing the team championship.
car3523.hero: A DTM machine with two victories in the Class 1 era.

car3524.desc: This homologation model of the R32 Skyline GT-R was produced in a limited run of just 500 units. With Group A victory as its target, engineers implemented comprehensive cooling enhancements, replaced the turbocharger’s turbine with a more durable metal unit, and reworked the body to optimize aerodynamics while shedding unnecessary weight. The result was a marked increase in performance, propelling the car to numerous touring car victories not only in Japan, but also across Europe and Australia.
car3524.hero: A homologation model with 500 cars produced for Group A racing

car3525.desc: In 1965, this legendary machine delivered Honda its first-ever F1 victory. Building upon the foundation of the RA271—Honda’s first F1 challenger—this car achieved greater performance through weight reduction across its components, the adoption of outboard rear suspension, and refined tuning of its 1.5-liter V-12. Although early in the season it grappled with stability issues, significant improvements were introduced midway through the campaign. These efforts culminated in a hard-fought and celebrated triumph at Round 10, the Mexican Grand Prix.
car3525.hero: The F1 machine that scored Honda its first F1 victory.

car3526.desc: This striking machine was the winner of the 2017 Gran Turismo Award. Based on a 1992 EG Honda Civic, it features a PANDEM wide-body kit and a carbon-fiber hood inspired by a design from J's Racing. The interior has been fully stripped to reduce weight, and the original engine has been replaced with a K24 inline-4. This car stood as a striking symbol of the JDM (Japanese Domestic Market) scene.
car3526.hero: A time attack Civic customized in the classic JDM style.

car3528.desc: The Dallara SF23 Super Formula made its debut in the spring of 2023 as the latest machine for the Super Formula series. Developed under the “SUPER FORMULA NEXT50” initiative, the car aimed to promote sustainability in motorsports. It incorporated biocomposite materials, while significantly reducing CO₂ emissions. Engines were supplied by Toyota and Honda.
car3528.hero: The next evolution of Super Formula cars aims to bring sustainability to motorsports

car3529.desc: The Dallara SF23 Super Formula made its debut in the spring of 2023 as the latest machine for the Super Formula series. Developed under the “SUPER FORMULA NEXT50” initiative, the car aimed to promote sustainability in motorsports. It incorporated biocomposite materials, while significantly reducing CO₂ emissions. Engines were supplied by Toyota and Honda.
car3529.hero: The next evolution of Super Formula cars aims to bring sustainability to motorsports

car3530.desc: Introduced in 1962, Alfa Romeo’s first Giulia series began as a 4-door sedan, with the Sprint GT coupe joining the lineup in 1963. Designed by Giugiaro, the body featured elegant lines and subtly curved surfaces. The Sprint GT quickly gained popularity as a high-performance sports coupe and remained in production until 1977.
car3530.hero: An iconic 1960s high-performance coupe from Alfa Romeo
car3530.nameLong: Alfa Romeo Giulia Sprint GT Veloce '67

car3531.desc: This FIA-homologated GT3 race car was based on the AMG GT. While performance and aerodynamics were improved, development also prioritized reducing running costs for client teams. This led to longer engine life, improved radiator protection, and several other enhancements. In 2020, the EVO model was introduced alongside a facelift for the road car, bringing with it a host of new features.
car3531.hero: An improved and more cost effective GT3 machine

car3532.desc: The Valkyrie hypercar was the result of a collaboration between Red Bull Racing and Aston Martin. Its front wing was suspended beneath a high-nose front section, while the entire underbody functioned as an aerodynamic tunnel, generating immense downforce. Power came from a naturally-aspirated 6.5-liter V-12 paired with a KERS hybrid system. With a total system output of 1139 HP, the Valkyrie delivered performance on par with top-tier racing machines.
car3532.hero: A uniquely shaped hypercar with F1-derived aerodynamics.

car3533.desc: This marked Maserati’s first mid-engine sports car in 15 years, following the MC12. Designed with Dallara, the streamlined body was engineered to generate significant downforce without relying heavily on external aerodynamic elements. At its core was a lightweight carbon monocoque chassis weighing less than 220 lbs, paired with a newly developed twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine, featuring F1–inspired pre-chamber combustion.
car3533.hero: A special super car that embodies the tradition and passion of Maserati.

car3534.desc: Since the 1950s, Toyota had been producing ambulances based on specially adapted passenger and commercial vehicles. The most recent of these was the third-generation Himedic, a high-standard ambulance introduced in 2006. Its platform was built on the 200 Series HiAce Super Long. With improvements such as an expanded patient compartment, this vehicle was engineered for maximum functionality in critical, life-saving situations.
car3534.hero: Saving lives faster and more safely.

car3535.desc: The GR Corolla was developed by Toyota’s high-performance GR division as a hot hatch aimed squarely at outperforming its rivals. Already the most powerful model in Corolla history, it was taken even further with the hardcore MORIZO Edition. At a time when the automotive world moves toward electrification and advanced systems, the GR Corolla stood out as a rare celebration of the pure, mechanical thrill of the internal combustion engine.
car3535.hero: A 2-seat model that takes the GR Corolla to the extreme.

car3536.desc: The sixth-generation Honda Civic Type R was unveiled in September 2022. It was based on the FL 5-door hatchback variant of the 11th-generation Civic. Powering the car was a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 K20C engine, delivering 325.4 HP and 309.6 ft-lb of torque, surpassing the previous generation in both output and response. Updates to the 4-wheel independent active damper system further enhanced chassis performance, sharpening the car’s dynamic capability on both road and track.
car3536.hero: Driving feel comes first. The legendary R badge returns for the 11th generation Civic.

car3537.desc: This GT Original draws inspiration from the MAZDA3 Bio concept that competed in the ST-Q class of Japan’s Super Endurance Series. It runs on next-generation 100-percent biodiesel fuel derived from waste cooking oil. The body also incorporates environmentally friendly hybrid materials. This ambitious project aims to merge carbon neutrality with top-tier race car performance.
car3537.hero: Exploring the potential of internal combustion, a next-generation bio-diesel-powered race car.

car3538.desc: Introduced in 1966, the Dodge Charger was Chrysler’s response to the muscle car wave that swept across the United States during the 1960s. It quickly gained popularity for its laid-back styling and the widespread availability of powerful, large-displacement V-8s across the lineup. In 1968, the high-performance R/T (Road/Track) variant was introduced, featuring upgraded suspension and brakes, along with the option of the legendary 426 Hemi engine.
car3538.hero: This true 1960s muscle car is the envy of collectors everywhere.

car3539.desc: The Porsche 911 GT3 RS (992) was a high-performance road car that incorporated aerodynamic components from the 911 GT3 R race car. It was fitted with a range of advanced aerodynamic systems, including a large swan-neck rear wing with DRS (drag reduction system) and an active diffuser that functioned as an air brake under hard braking.
car3539.hero: A hyper-performance road car packed with race car features.

car3540.desc: The Tesla Model 3 is a compact battery-electric sedan. At the top of the lineup sat the Performance Dual Motor AWD variant, capable of accelerating from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.3 seconds and reaching a top speed of 162.2 mph. Under WLTP testing—the global standard for electric and fuel efficiency—it offered an impressive maximum range of 339.9 miles. In 2023, it received its first major update, introducing refinements to the front fascia, overall length, and interior controls.
car3540.hero: A best-seller from the company that changed the EV market forever.

car3541.desc: The BVLGARI Aluminium Vision Gran Turismo draws its inspiration from the "BVLGARI Aluminium," a watch that reshaped the industry in 1998, carrying the same spirit—sporty, intelligent, essential and precise. Its design remains timeless and distinctive, reflecting a bold, conceptual approach while staying true to BVLGARI’s design DNA, rising above fleeting trends and fashion cycles.
car3541.hero: A digital concept car infused with the DNA of BVLGARI.

car3542.desc: With more than 130 years of heritage, Czech manufacturer Škoda made its Gran Turismo debut with a single-seater EV producing 800kW (1071 HP). The exterior design blended styling cues from Škoda’s classic forebears with a host of advanced technologies, including independent left and right rear wings that respond to driving conditions. It also incorporates onboard distance sensors that assess the position of other vehicles.
car3542.hero: A single-seat all-wheel-drive EV from the distinguished Czech manufacturer.

car3543.desc: The Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept embodies the pinnacle of the brand’s design philosophy. It features Genesis’ signature anti-wedge profile, introducing fresh design ideas for future sports models. Powered by the Lambda II V-6 with electric assist, it produces 1,071 hp (1071 HP). It represents a perfect balance of sculpted beauty and raw performance.
car3543.hero: A sports coupe that embodies the athletic elegance sought by Genesis.
car3543.nameLong: Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept
car3543.nameShort: Genesis X Gran Berlinetta VGT Concept

car3544.desc: The Genesis X Gran Racer Vision Gran Turismo Concept is the ultimate expression of Genesis’ "Athletic Elegance." This Racer version dramatically increases downforce to enhance lap times. Its hybrid powertrain paired a V-6 engine with electric assists to deliver a staggering 1518.7 HP and 1,015 ft-lb (1014.8 ft-lb) of torque.
car3544.hero: The racing version of the Gran Berlinetta adorned with aerodynamic parts.
car3544.nameLong: Genesis X Gran Racer Vision Gran Turismo Concept
car3544.nameShort: Genesis X Gran Racer VGT Concept

car3545.desc: This was Japan’s premier micro off-roader. Since its debut in the 1970s, the Jimny consistently adhered to kei-car regulations, featuring a ladder frame chassis, 4-wheel drive with rigid axle suspension, and large-diameter tires. In 2018, the boxy fourth-generation model was introduced, maintaining its rugged charm while gaining popularity both as a leisure vehicle and as a reliable workhorse in Japan’s mountainous regions.
car3545.hero: Japan's mighty micro off-roader boasts amazing all-terrain ability beyond its size.

car3546.desc: The AFEELA Prototype 2024 was a BEV introduced by Sony Honda Mobility during CES® 2024. An array of sensing technologies delivered intuitive driver assistance, while dashboard and rear-seat displays offered abundant in-car entertainment. AFEELA turned the notion of waiting during travel into an enjoyable experience.
car3546.hero: A revolutionary "mobility device" set to change how we spend time commuting.

car3547.desc: The Renault 4 (Quatre), introduced in 1961, was designed to replace the best-selling 4CV. By 1978, the car reached its full potential with the GTL variant. This model added a plastic grille, a more powerful 1.1-liter engine, and a modernized instrument panel. Amassing more than 8.1 million units by the end of its production in 1992, the Renault 4 became a French cultural icon. It was a car for the people, a symbol of practical, efficient design from France.
car3547.hero: The world's first hatchback found great success through utilitarian design.

car3548.desc: Introduced in 2018, the Urus was Lamborghini’s high-performance SUV. It marked the brand’s first use of forced induction, powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 capable of accelerating from zero to 62.1 mph in 3.6 seconds, and reaching a top speed of 189.5 mph—a record at the time of its debut. Equipped with active air suspension, rear-wheel steering, and a torque vectoring system, it delivered exceptional handling and cornering capabilities uncommon in vehicles of its class.
car3548.hero: Lamborghini's take on a high-performance exotic SUV.

car3549.desc: The Volvo 240 Estate became synonymous with the Swedish brand's image as a station wagon maker. Its boxy shape and long profile became design signatures that made the vehicle popular to all. Inside, it offered a minimalist Scandinavian interior with plush, sofa-like seating. Its production run ended in 1993, but the 240 remains a beloved classic, still seen in daily use, a rarity among vintage cars.
car3549.hero: A historic model that epitomized the station wagon.

car3550.desc: This WRC machine was based on the 2-door Impreza. Beginning with the 1997 model, this evolution introduced computer-controlled active differentials at the front, rear, and center. Although it didn’t secure Subaru a fourth consecutive constructors’ title, Colin McRae’s wins in Portugal, the Tour de Corse, and the Acropolis rallies proved its formidable potential.
car3550.hero: Subaru's triple race winning Impreza World Rally car from the 1998 season.

car3551.desc: The second-generation M3 was based on the E36 3 Series. It marked a shift from pure motorsport focus to a more refined grand tourer. This model offered a broader appeal with multiple body styles, including a 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, and cabriolet. Originally equipped with a 3.0-liter engine, the M3 received an upgrade in 1995 to a 3.2-liter unit, along with the introduction of a 6-speed manual and an optional 2-pedal SMG (Sequential Manual Gearbox).
car3551.hero: From race car to luxury grand tourer, the second-generation M3.

car3553.desc: The arrival of the 2024 GT-R silenced speculation that production had ended with the 2022 model. A newly designed exhaust silencer allowed the car to meet noise regulations without compromising performance. Aerodynamic refinements enhanced downforce. Also, the addition of high-sensitivity G-sensors in the electronically controlled suspension improved both traction and ride comfort, elevating the GT-R’s performance and refinement to new heights.
car3553.hero: News of the Nissan GT-R R35's demise was evidently greatly exaggerated.

car3554.desc: The Hiace has long stood as Toyota’s flagship commercial vehicle, earning widespread support around the globe. Introduced in 2004 and continually refined, the fifth-generation H200 model became a record-setting seller. Offered in various configurations based on body size, it came with a choice of 2.0-liter or 2.7-liter gasoline engines, or a 2.8-liter diesel engine. The Van DX variant featured a standard roof height and rear-wheel drive. It accommodated up to nine passengers, or, with the seats folded, transforming into a spacious cargo carrier.
car3554.hero: The cab-over commercial van was equally capable of moving people and cargo.

car3555.desc: Introduced in 1992, the Escort RS Cosworth was a homologation model built to support Ford’s campaign in the WRC. It inherited the 2.0-liter twin-cam engine from the Sierra, producing 223.9 HP, and featured a 4-wheel-drive system that delivered exceptional rally performance. The car proved its capability with a 1-2 finish at the Rally de Portugal, followed by back-to-back victories in the Tour de Corse and Acropolis Rally, firmly reestablishing Ford as a force in the world of rallying.
car3555.hero: A WRC homologation special with a unique double-decker wing design.

car3556.desc: The Unimog was a commercial vehicle developed and sold by Daimler Truck. First produced in 1948, it went on to become a long-running success as a highly versatile, multi-purpose machine. Introduced in 1956, the 411 series served as its successor, featuring a more powerful engine and a reinforced body structure. With three available wheelbase options and a variety of body styles, the lineup included twelve distinct models, each of which could be further customized with a wide range of attachments.
car3556.hero: The benchmark for versatile, high-mobility vehicles.

car3557.desc: The W 196 was developed by Mercedes-Benz in anticipation of the new F1 regulations shifting to 2.5-liter engines from 1954. The W 196 R variant was specifically constructed for competition in F1. Its 2496 cc inline-8 engine produced 285 HP and was capable of reaching a top speed of 180.2 mph. The car delivered outstanding results during the 1954 and 1955 Formula One World Championships, with driver Juan Manuel Fangio securing the drivers' title in both seasons.
car3557.hero: A legendary F1 car that made motorsports history.

car3558.desc: Having stood as the symbol of the Porsche brand since the 1960s, the 911 entered its eighth generation in 2018 with the Type 992. In April 2020, Porsche introduced the Turbo S variant to the 992 lineup as its top-performing model. Powered by a twin-turbocharged 3745 cc flat-6 engine, the Turbo S delivered 641 HP and 590.2 ft-lb of torque, channeled through all four wheels, enabling a 0–62.1 mph time of just 2.7 seconds and a top speed of 205.1 mph.
car3558.hero: The top performance version of the eighth-generation 911.

car3559.desc: This 3-door model of the Jimny was lengthened and widened to better suit international markets. Now mated to a 1460 cc DOHC inline-4, the part-time 4WD system with a mechanical transfer case delivers uncompromising off-road performance. The third-generation JB74, counting from the original Sierra, earned widespread acclaim for its boxy, elongated design.
car3559.hero: A stouter Jimny with an eye on global success.

car3560.desc: This all-electric hypercar was unveiled on June 8, 2023—exactly 75 years after the original Porsche 356 "No.1" Roadster received approval. Its exterior design incorporated motifs from Porsche’s storied racing heritage, while the cockpit focused entirely on the driver experience. This car achieved a power-to-weight ratio of 1 horsepower per 2 lbs and downforce far exceeding that of the 992-generation 911 GT3 RS.
car3560.hero: A hypercar concept to celebrate the 75th anniversary of Porsche.

car3561.desc: This performance model was introduced two years after the original launch of the IONIQ 5. It featured a 4-wheel-drive system powered by electric motors on the front and rear axles, allowing for freely adjustable torque distribution. When set to a rear-wheel bias, the system enabled the over two-ton SUV to be drifted with ease. In an effort to preserve the excitement of traditional combustion-engine cars, this unique electric SUV also offered a simulated 8-speed dual-clutch transmission and synthetic exhaust sounds.
car3561.hero: A fearsome driving machine that challenges the preconceptions of BEVs.

car3562.desc: The F3500-A, a Gran Turismo original, was born from a deep admiration for early 1990s Formula 1 machines. It was built around a carbon-fiber chassis and equipped with pushrod suspension. Its naturally-aspirated 3.5-liter V-12 screamed to 15,000 rpm and was paired with a 6-speed semiautomatic transmission. Formula cars continue to evolve. The F3500-A stands as a benchmark—an idealized representation of just how far performance and design had advanced during that era.
car3562.hero: An original formula car created in the image of classic F1 cars.

car3563.desc: In 1987, Honda introduced the all-new fourth-generation Civic. It was known as the Grand Civic, with the model code EF. Its most significant advancement was a complete platform overhaul, bringing double wishbone suspension to all four corners. The sporty Si model and the more luxurious Si Extra both featured the 1.6-liter DOHC ZC inline-4 engine. These models also found success on the track, competing in the Japan Touring Car Championship and securing championship titles.
car3563.hero: A dominating force on the touring car circuit, this fourth-generation Civic features the famous ZC engine.

car3564.desc: Peugeot introduced the 205 GTI as a spirited road-going counterpart to its 205 Turbo 16 WRC car. Its compact frame and punchy 1.6-liter SOHC engine delivered a thrilling, well-rounded driving experience. More than 300,000 units of this French masterpiece sold across Europe, securing its place in the pantheon of 1980s and 1990s car-culture history.
car3564.hero: A masterpiece hot hatch from France that became a rally legend.

car3565.desc: Following a series of internationally-focused models such as the Corolla and Yaris, Toyota introduced the C-HR crossover SUV in 2016, designed as a global vehicle for the modern era. This distinctive SUV also hinted at sporting ambitions, with a prototype version taking part in the Nürburgring 24 Hours race. Built on Toyota’s next-generation TNGA platform, the C-HR came with a choice of a 1.8-liter hybrid powertrain or a turbocharged 1.2-liter inline-4. The C-HR would go on to earn broad acclaim, becoming a bestseller.
car3565.hero: An unconventional crossover SUV that took on the Nürburgring 24 Hours.

car3566.desc: The CX-30 is a crossover SUV introduced to fill the gap between the CX-3 and CX-5. Although compact in size, it showcased Mazda's signature "KODO" design, evident in its sculpted front end and the way light flowed across its sleek body lines. In 2021, Mazda released the CX-30 X Smart Edition. This version featured the innovative SKYACTIV-X engine, paired with enhanced driver assistance systems and refined pedal feedback.
car3566.hero: This crossover SUV from Mazda featured a revolutionary engine design.

car3567.desc: In French, small vans are called "fourgonnettes." And the Kangoo gained popularity for embodying that spirit, with sliding passenger doors and split-folding rear seats that made it ideal not only for commercial tasks but also for personal and recreational use. It became a pioneer of the ludospace segment—vehicles designed for leisure activity. While its engine delivered only modest power, the soft suspension gave it a surprisingly lively and enjoyable driving character.
car3567.hero: This popular leisure activity vehicle began its life as a commercial van.

car3568.desc: Nissan’s Qashqai, a popular compact SUV that was introduced in 2006, entered its third generation with a bolder presence and a more refined design. Built on a larger platform, the new model showcased a more confident stance and featured Nissan’s innovative e-Power hybrid system. Unlike traditional hybrids, e-Power used a gasoline engine solely to generate electricity, which then powered the electric motors that drove the wheels, delivering an EV-like driving experience without the need to plug in. The Tekna trim came well-equipped, offering premium features such as larger alloy wheels, ambient interior lighting, and a sharp head-up display, all included as standard.
car3568.hero: Nissan's compact SUV is even better with e-Power.

car3569.desc: The Nismp R34 GT-R Z-tune stood as the ultimate expression of Nissan’s tuning prowess — a fully re-engineered, limited-production masterpiece based on the R34 Skyline GT-R.  Under the hood, the standard RB26DETT engine was replaced with a 2.8-liter version of the RB26DETT Kai-Z2, derived from Nissan’s GT500 race program. Nismo reinforced the chassis with additional spot welds and strategically integrated carbon fiber components, while fine-tuning the suspension and braking systems to deliver razor-sharp performance. The result was a road-going GT-R with motorsport DNA baked into every detail. Including the original prototype, only 19 units were ever built, making the Z-tune one of the rarest and most revered GT-Rs ever created.
car3569.hero: This GT-R bows out with the ultimate complete tuned model.

car3570.desc: The Corvette C5 lineup expanded in 1999 with the addition of a hardtop model, which increased body rigidity and improved performance. Even more appealing to enthusiasts was its lower price point compared to the standard model, which helped it gain strong support. In 2001, Chevrolet pushed the C5 platform even further with the Z06. Inspired by the spirit of the C2, it delivered outstanding performance and held the highest top speed of any production Corvette of its time.
car3570.hero: The top-of-the-line variant of the fifth-generation Corvette revives the classic Z06 moniker.

car3571.desc: Japan’s micro-car segment, known locally as kei-cars, has become an indispensable part of everyday life throughout the country. The Suzuki Carry compact truck is a classic example of the commercial kei-car segment, which includes a wide range of cargo vans and mini trucks. Introduced in 1961, the Carry has built a long-standing reputation. The model shown here is the 2012 version, the final evolution of the 10th generation. With its endearing styling and everyday practicality, the Carry has begun to attract attention from enthusiasts and users overseas as well.
car3571.hero: A quintessential example of the micro-truck trend that has become a hit all over the world.

car3572.desc: In the 1990s, Honda introduced the “Creative Mover” category, launching the original CR-V in 1995 as part of that vision. By 2021, the fifth-generation CR-V had evolved significantly, with this model becoming the first in the series to feature a hybrid powertrain. A 4-wheel-drive option remained popular, offering added versatility. Its larger body improved interior space and expanded cargo capacity to over 1,100 liters. A 3-row, 7-seat configuration further enhanced practicality. Equipped with a wide range of safety features and advanced driver assistance systems, it proved to be an ideal vehicle for daily use.
car3572.hero: The fifth-generation model of this popular SUV is the first to feature a hybrid system.

car3573.desc: The BX made its debut at the 1982 Paris Salon. It carried forward the spirit of Citroën’s iconic GS and CX models while introducing a modern, geometric design language. The styling was penned by Marcello Gandini during his tenure at Bertone. True to Citroën tradition, the car featured the brand’s signature hydropneumatic suspension system. The 19 TRS model featured here was a grand tourer-style variant powered by a 1.9-liter gasoline engine.
car3573.hero: Citroën’s versatile tourer receives a modern makeover.

car3574.desc: The Peugeot 2008 was introduced in 2013. This featured 2008 SUV is a second-generation model. It was built on the same platform as Peugeot’s 208 hatchback. The lighting elements featured motifs inspired by a lion’s claws and fangs. One of the most notable features of this compact SUV was the 3D i-Cockpit, which included a small-diameter steering wheel with flattened top and bottom sections, paired with a head-up digital instrument cluster positioned above it for optimal driver visibility.
car3574.hero: This compact SUV showcases Peugeot design cues throughout.

car3575.desc: The FIAT Panda is a front-wheel-drive hatchback introduced in 1980, born amid the compact-car boom that followed the oil crises. Its design was penned by the master stylist Giorgetto Giugiaro. To keep costs low, the body was crafted with straight lines and flat panels, achieving a look that was both practical and modern. At launch, buyers could choose between an air-cooled 652 cc 2-cylinder engine or a water-cooled 903 cc 4-cylinder unit. The model featured in Gran Turismo is the former.
car3575.hero: This jewel of a compact car is the one designer Giugiaro called his greatest work.

car3576.desc: Honda’s N-ONE was a retro-inspired kei-car that paid homage to the company's first entry into the segment, the classic N360. The second-generation model retained the charming silhouette of the original, but rode on a completely new chassis that brought modern refinement to its compact dimensions. Among the highlights of the lineup was the RS trim, a sporty variant that borrowed close-ratio gearing from the S660 sports car. It featured reinforced synchronizers for second and third gear, and a heavy-duty clutch to handle spirited driving. While the RS badge had been offered on the first-gen N-ONE, the new RS stood out as the first kei-car to pair a turbocharged, front-wheel-drive layout with a 6-speed manual transmission — a groundbreaking move in the world of Japan’s smallest cars.
car3576.hero: This performance-focused model is a first kei-car with front-wheel drive, a turbocharged engine and a 6-speed manual transmission.

car3577.desc: The Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo is a fully electric high-performance concept car that blends Opel’s respect for tradition with its passion for futuristic technology. Twin electric motors, one mounted on each axle, delivers a combined output of 588 kW (788 HP). This enables the car to accelerate from 0-62.1 mph in just two seconds and reach a top speed of 198.8 mph. Its aerodynamic performance is equally impressive, with an active aero diffuser and spoiler that ensures stability even at the highest speeds.
car3577.hero: This Vision Gran Turismo embodies the electric spirit of Opel’s GSE sports car brand.
car3577.nameLong: Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo

car3578.desc: This machine was created by Mazda Spirit Racing, an initiative launched in 2021 to embody Mazda’s motorsport ambitions. Although derived from the ND Roadster, it has a 2.0-liter block not typically offered on Japanese soft-top models, distinguished by specially developed camshafts, a bespoke cylinder head, forged pistons, and a custom exhaust manifold. This delivers an output of 197.2 HP, a figure that stands near the upper limit of what remains practical in a production car. Additional refinements were made throughout the chassis, drawing upon the wealth of expertise Mazda had accumulated through years of Super Endurance racing.
car3578.hero: With only 200 units ever produced, this is the ultimate works-tuned roadster.

car3579.desc: The AFEELA 1 was unveiled at CES® 2025. This production model was offered in two distinct trims—Origin and Signature. The cabin was envisioned as a Creative Entertainment Space that challenged traditional notions of what travel could be. Advanced technologies were embedded throughout the BEV, including an array of external sensing devices and an intelligent personal agent capable of holding natural, conversational dialogue.
car3579.hero: A new era of mobility that reimagines transportation.

car3581.desc: The Corvette CX Concept was an all-wheel drive electric hypercar. At its core was a fan-powered downforce system, using fighter jet–style thrust vectoring to precisely balance aerodynamic forces between the front and rear.  This advanced setup allowed for more than 2,000 horsepower generated by four electric motors. Engineered to feel equally at home on both road and track, the CX Concept represented a bold new vision for the Corvette legacy.
car3581.hero: An electric hypercar that offered a glimpse into the future of the Corvette.

car3582.desc: The Corvette CX.R Vision Gran Turismo Concept is a track-only model based on the Corvette CX Concept. With enhanced aerodynamics and a dramatically lower ride height, it offers even greater performance capability. Under the skin, a hybrid powertrain combines electric motors with an e-fuel–driven engine, delivering the speed, endurance, and efficiency demanded by endurance racing.
car3582.hero: A futuristic GT racer born from the Corvette lineage.
car3582.nameLong: Chevrolet Corvette CX.R Vision Gran Turismo Concept

car3583.desc: When it was introduced in 1994, the Toyota RAV4 pioneered an entirely new market segment, called the “crossover SUV.” With its compact body and high ground clearance, it quickly gained followers around the world and reached its fifth generation in 2018. The Adventure grade brought rugged off-road styling, highlighted by a custom grille, skid-plate bumpers, and 19-inch wheel rims. A 2.0-liter inline-4 Dynamic Force Engine was mated to a Direct Shift-CVT, delivering smooth acceleration and impressive fuel efficiency.
car3583.hero: An adventurous SUV for active lifestyles.

car3584.desc: Renowned for its all-terrain performance and reliability, the Toyota Land Cruiser has become among the world’s most beloved off-road vehicles. Introduced in 1960, the third-generation “40” series also offered a surprising degree of on-road comfort. The 2-door hardtop variant shown here was powered by a 3.9-liter F-model gasoline engine, paired with a part-time 4-wheel-drive system. Its popularity only grew in 1974 with the introduction of the 3.0-liter B-model diesel engine. The 40 series went on to become a massive success, remaining in production until 1984.
car3584.hero: A best-selling Land Cruiser with a 24-year production run.

car3585.desc: Introduced as the high-performance model of the seventh-generation ELANTRA, the ELANTRA N was developed to embody the N brand philosophy of “making cornering fun.” Powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine producing 276.1 HP and 289.3 ft-lb of torque, it accelerated from 0-62.1 mph in just 5.3 seconds, despite its front-wheel-drive layout. It was offered with either a 6-speed manual transmission or an 8-speed DCT. Its running gear featured electronically controlled dampers and an eLSD, complemented by a robust braking system.
car3585.hero: This track-ready Elantra is brought to you by the letter "N."

car3586.desc: Created by the Scandinavian electric performance brand Polestar, the Polestar 5 is an all-wheel-drive electric sedan distinguished by its sleek, sub-five-meter profile and a glass roof that extends gracefully to the rear. Power came from a dual-motor setup, with one motor mounted on each axle. In Performance trim, it delivered an impressive 650 kW and 1,015 Nm of torque. Its 800-volt electrical architecture supported 350 kW rapid charging, replenishing the battery from 10 to 80 percent in just 22 minutes. Under WLTP testing, the dual-motor version achieved a maximum range of 416.3 miles.
car3586.hero: Polestar's flagship model combines sustainability with high-performance.

car3587.desc: The 296 GTB itself was a plug-in hybrid and the first Ferrari to feature a V-6 engine since the iconic Dino series. The smallest member of Ferrari’s current lineup, its beautifully sculpted body paid homage to the 250 LM of the 1960s. Power came from a mid-mounted twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine paired with a 123 kW electric motor, producing a combined output of 830 horsepower. Capable of accelerating from 0-62.1 mph in just 2.9 seconds and reaching 205.1 mph at full stride, the 296 GTB delivered the breathtaking performance worthy of the Ferrari name.
car3587.hero: Here's a mid-engine sports car with a revolutionary V-6 + PHEV system.

car3588.desc: Derived from the 296 GTB, the 296 GT3 was a purebred race machine that shed the plug-in hybrid system of the road car, relying solely on a 600-horsepower twin-turbocharged V-6 engine. Built by world-renowned constructor Oreca, the car was crafted with meticulous precision—from chassis construction and assembly to customer support. After its debut at the 24 Hours of Spa in July 2022, it quickly demonstrated its exceptional racing prowess, achieving 100 victories in less than two years.
car3588.hero: This elegant GT3 machine is also known as the "Racing Queen."

car3589.desc: The F3500-A was conceived as a tribute to the early 1990s Formula 1 race cars, and the F3500-B proudly carries that legacy forward. Its most significant evolution lies in the powertrain. While the F3500-A was powered by a V-12, the F3500-B adopts a compact, lightweight V-8. Although smaller in displacement, this engine revs to an astonishing 13,800 rpm, generating more than 700.2 HP in the process. The F3500-B also offers three distinct front wing configurations for its high-nose layout.
car3589.hero: Here's a V-8 version of the GT original formula car.

car3590.desc: The Hyundai ELANTRA N TC was a special model built for racing. Based on the ELANTRA N, which could accelerate from 0–62.1 mph in just 5.3 seconds despite using a front-wheel-drive layout, the TC model was specially outfitted according to touring-car race regulations. The wide body was equipped with a carbon-fiber splitter and a large rear wing to greatly improve high-speed cornering stability. This model was also fitted with a 6-speed sequential gearbox, with the braking and cooling parts upgraded to endurance-racing standards.
car3590.hero: This track-oriented Elantra was meticulously crafted to achieve victory.

car3591.desc: Ten years after the debut of Europe’s first minivan came the Renault Espace F1—an unprecedented creation that redefined the limits of imagination. At its heart resided the RS4 3.5-liter V-10 from the 1992 Formula 1 championship–winning FW14B, mounted amidships within a body crafted from aluminum and carbon fiber. Producing 788 HP, it rocketed from 0-62.1 mph in just 2.8 seconds and reached a top speed of 196.4 mph. This extraordinary machine was even driven on a real circuit by F1 legend Alain Prost, among others.
car3591.hero: Renault's rebellious minivan carries an F1 engine.

car3592.desc: The Chevrolet Camaro 1968 Race-Mod was Gran Turismo’s modern interpretation of the Camaro Z28, a car originally developed for homologation in the SCCA’s Trans-Am Series. Adorned with carbon black trim, the exterior featured a wide-mouth bumper, a large ducktail spoiler, and a center-exit exhaust. The interior featured a sequential shifter and roll cage, along with Alcantara bucket seats.
car3592.hero: This is a restomod of the classic Trans-Am hero Camaro Z28.

car3599.desc: The Xiaomi SU7 Ultra was an extreme performance version of the first car from smart device maker Xiaomi, the SU7 sports sedan. The all-wheel-drive system, which used three electric motors spread across the front and rear axles, boasted a total system output of 1526.6 HP. The "V8" model motors located on the rear axle were the most powerful in any production car, able to rotate at speeds of up to 27,200 rpm. Also, extensive aerodynamic development resulted in the car being able to produce up to 628 lbs of downforce.
car3599.hero: It's the smartphone giant’s expression of automotive innovation.

car36.desc: The Chevelle was introduced in 1964 as Chevrolet’s first intermediate-size model. The Chevelle also offered the "SS" performance trim, which reached its peak with the introduction of the 1970 model. That year saw the debut of the SS 454, powered by the LS6 engine, the most powerful production engine listed in any American car catalog at the time. It's no wonder that the SS 454 quickly became one of the most formidable and dependable contenders on the drag racing circuit.
car36.hero: A massive engine that produced plenty of power made this car a favorite for drag racing.

car3600.desc: The 911 GT3 R was a pure racing machine developed from the 992-model 911, the eighth generation of Porsche’s everyday sports car. Introduced in 2022, this machine was equipped with a naturally aspirated 4.2-liter flat-6 engine, producing a maximum 557.2 HP. It also featured lightweight carbon body panels and aramid-fiber components, as well as the double-wishbone/multilink suspension setup derived from the 911 RSR.
car3600.hero: This is a pure racing machine from the 8th generation 911 catalogue.

car3601.desc: The Captur was a compact crossover SUV produced by Renault. The second-generation model, introduced in 2019, measured 13.9 ft in length, 5.9 ft in width and 5.2 ft in height, giving it the stance of an SUV while preserving the agility of a compact car. It offered a broad range of powertrain options, spanning conventional gasoline engines as well as diesel and hybrid variants. Most notable among them was the E-Tech PHEV system, which incorporated hybrid technology developed by Renault’s Formula 1 team.
car3601.hero: A formidable vehicle that blurred the boundaries of the compact SUV class.

car3602.desc: Released by Yangwang, BYD’s luxury brand, the U9 is a supercar aimed at delivering the ultimate in power, technology and speed in the electric era. It uses the proprietary e⁴ platform, featuring four electric motors that produce a total system output of 960 kW, or roughly 1286 HP. It accelerates from 0-62.1 mph in 2.36 seconds. In 2025, the high-performance U9 Xtreme variant attempted to set a world speed record, reaching 308.3 mph.
car3602.hero: This rare electric super car broke world speed records.

car3603.desc: The Twingo became known for its 3-door monospace design, with a near-continuous curve flowing from the truncated hood, over the roof and into the rear. The wheels were positioned at the extreme corners of the body, allowing for an unusually spacious interior despite its compact form. At launch, the engine delivered modest output, but paired with the lightweight body, it provided a lively and engaging drive in urban settings. It was also praised for bringing character to a practical vehicle, with sliding rear seats that enabled a variety of seating/cargo configurations.
car3603.hero: Practical yet cute. A breath of fresh air for the A-segment.

car3604.desc: This cutting-edge Le Mans Daytona h (LMDh) prototype used a Dallara-built carbon-fiber monocoque and a hybrid system built around the DTM-derived P66/3, a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 engine. During the 2025 season, the car competed in both the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and the FIA World Endurance Championship, highlighted by a 1-2 finish at Road America in the eighth round of IMSA In the WEC, it also showed strong pace at rounds such as Imola, proving itself at the highest level of endurance racing.
car3604.hero: A new category sports prototype that carries the lineage of the celebrated V12 LMR.

car3605.desc: The Ferrari 499P was a prototype developed for the Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) category. Its advanced hybrid all-wheel-drive system combined a twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine with a front-mounted MGU to produce a total output of 500kW. Upon Ferrari’s return to Le Mans in 2023, the car went up against a field of its strongest rivals and came out on top, securing overall victory. This would mark Ferrari’s first victory at Le Mans in 58 years.
car3605.hero: The glorious Prancing Horse that returned Ferrari to the top category and delivered victory at Le Mans after a 50-year absence.

car3606.desc: Peugeot returned to the top class of endurance racing under Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) regulations in 2022 after previously stepping away in 2011. Its return was marked by the arrival of the all-wheel-drive hybrid 9X8. The original aerodynamic concept eliminated the need for a rear wing, although one was introduced as part of the car’s 2024 evolution package. The 2025 version further refined those developments, resulting in the most complete form of the 9X8. It demonstrated its potential with a 2nd place finish at Fuji during the 2025 FIA World Endurance Championship season.
car3606.hero: An electric hypercar that represents the racing spirit of Peugeot.

car3607.desc: Porsche’s Le Mans Daytona h (LMDh) contender, the 963, carried forward the legacy of the legendary 962 and 919 Hybrid. After making its debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona, it quickly amassed victories and podiums in IMSA and the WEC before Porsche claimed both the Drivers’ and Manufacturers’ titles in the 2024 IMSA season. For 2025, the car received further development in its suspension and rear aerodynamic package to improve balance and stability on any circuit.
car3607.hero: A new category LMDh hypercar created by Porsche, the masters of endurance.

car3608.desc: This 992-generation Porsche 911 Turbo S was a virtual model created by Gran Turismo and reimagined as a safety car. Built on Porsche’s updated 911 platform, the wide-body design incorporated a higher percentage of aluminum components. Its exceptional traction and stability made the 911 Turbo ideally suited for leading the field as a safety car.
car3608.hero: The 911 Turbo S reimagined as a safety car.

car3609.desc: This was an evolution of the GT3 CONCEPT racing car based on the MAZDA RX-VISION, which was unveiled in 2015. The splitter, diffuser and rear wing were redesigned to improve aerodynamic performance and increase downforce. Front canards were added, along with revisions to the grille mesh and the shape of the rear body panels. The front tire size was also changed to significantly improve cornering ability, a crucial factor in racing.
car3609.hero: The RX-VISION GT3 evolved for serious competition.

car3610.desc: This was the second high-performance EV from Hyundai N. Equipped with a power unit with 770 Nm of torque and 641 HP of total system output, in a body tuned for aerodynamic performance, it accelerates from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.2 seconds. Features such as N Active Sound+ and N e-Shift, which gave the feeling of gear shifts in an EV, showed Hyundai N’s dedication to preserving the fun of driving.
car3610.hero: A new paradigm for high-performance EV.

car3611.desc: The Tourer V was a performance model added to the eighth-generation Mark II lineup. Its biggest selling point was its power unit: a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-6 engine that produced 276.1 HP and 278.5 ft-lb of torque. A 5-speed manual transmission was also available, and the roar of the 6-cylinder engine, combined with tremendous boost, hit as soon as the throttle pedal was floored. Even so, the interior was lavish and comfortable, bringing two seemingly opposite characters together in the Tourer V.
car3611.hero: This sports sedan's refined looks hide sharp teeth.

car3612.desc: The Chaser was Toyota’s midsize sedan, sharing the Mark II’s fundamental design but wearing different exterior styling. The Tourer V performance model was powered by the second-generation 1JZ-GTE engine with variable valve timing, and flooring the pedal launched this beast forward with ferocious boost. The front-engine/rear-wheel-drive layout provided excellent control, making the car responsive to the driver’s inputs.
car3612.hero: This sister to the Toyota Mark II provides an intense drive.

car365.desc: The 155 2.5 V6 TI was Alfa Romeo’s answer to the increasingly advanced Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters (DTM), which, by 1993, allowed significant car modifications. Based on the 1992 155 sedan, it featured a 60-degree 2.5-liter V-6 powerplant producing 414.2 HP and a full-time 4-wheel-drive system. The car won 12 of 20 rounds and secured the championship.
car365.hero: This champion race car won 12 out of 20 races in the super-competitive DTM race series.

car3653.desc: France's world-famous economy car, the 2 CV remained in production for 42 years after its introduction in 1948. Introduced in 1980, the Charleston was a special-edition model featuring a two-tone body and a more luxurious interior. At its heart was an air-cooled flat-2 engine that had grown to 602 cc over the generations, and while it produced just 28.6 HP, that was enough to propel the extremely lightweight body with ease.
car3653.hero: A masterpiece of the French people's car with a two-tone color scheme.

car3654.desc: This mid-engine sports car featured a Pininfarina-designed body that perfectly blended flowing lines with functional beauty. Its naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V-8 produced 107.5 HP per liter, an extraordinary achievement for its time. Its superb weight balance and cutting-edge electronically controlled suspension gave it handling that helped establish the car as one of the great masterpieces in Ferrari history.
car3654.hero: A masterpiece new generation midship, that inherits the passion of the 348.

car3655.desc: The sixth-generation Step WGN minivan featured a low floor and large sliding doors, creating an extremely practical package that earned widespread support from families. Of the many versions in the lineup, the Spada Premium Line was the most luxurious, featuring exclusive platinum-style chrome trim, a high-quality dark-toned interior and a 7-seat layout with second-row captain's chairs for exceptional comfort.
car3655.hero: This upper-grade version of the sixth-generation Step WGN, with improvements in driving performance, space and refinement.
car3655.nameLong: Honda Step WGN Spada Premium Line '23

car3656.desc: This electric hypercar featured a teardrop-shaped cockpit embedded within a body sculpted with cutouts and air ducts. Its signature halo-shaped taillight served as both a visual icon and a massive air outlet. Together with numerous aerodynamic innovations, the car achieved a drag coefficient of 0.29, downforce of -1.2 and an aerodynamic efficiency rating of 4.1. Achieving both low drag and high downforce is a difficult aerodynamic challenge, but this car managed to balance the two at an exceptionally high level.
car3656.hero: A Hypercar Sculpted by Wind and Intelligence.

car37.desc: The Civic is Honda’s longest-running model line. The fifth-generation EG Civic, introduced in September 1991, was promoted as the “sports Civic.” At the top of the range sat the SiR grade, equipped with a 1.6-liter DOHC VTEC engine. Building on the success of the previous SiR, which had already achieved the benchmark of 100 horsepower per liter, this model delivered an additional 9.9 HP, bringing total output to 167.7 HP.
car37.hero: The top-of-the-line fifth-generation Civic balances speed with comfort.

car374.desc: The FC3S, second generation of the RX-7, made its debut in October 1985. Sporting a sleek, futuristic design, it was shorter than its predecessor but both taller and wider. This new generation also carried an additional 441 lbs of weight. To offset the added weight, the FC3S was fitted with the newly developed 13B rotary engine. Each chamber was enlarged to 654 cc, and with the addition of a turbocharger, the engine delivered a peak output of 182.4 HP and 180.8 ft-lb of torque.
car374.hero: This version of the second-generation RX-7 offered better driver feedback and agility.

car379.desc: Released in September 1999, this was the coupe version of the Impreza Version VI. In addition to its rally-inspired styling, it came equipped with the Driver’s Control Center Differential (DCCD), an intercooler water sprayer, specially tuned stiff suspension, and a reinforced rear axle—all as standard. Its iconic EJ20 engine was tuned to deliver 276.1 HP, making this one of the most complete and refined GC8 models ever produced.
car379.hero: After six years of evolution, this car represented the final form of the GC8 Impreza coupe.
car379.nameLong: Subaru Impreza Coupe WRX Type R STi Version VI '99
car379.nameShort: Impreza Coupe WRX Type R STi Ver.VI '99

car387.desc: Daimler-Benz revealed the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL at the 1955 New York Auto Show. While its 161.6 mph top speed was impressive, its roof-hinged "gullwing" doors made it unforgettable, which allowed the car's doors to open upward. Only 1,400 gullwing Coupés were built from 1955 to 1957 before the model evolved into the 300 SL Roadster.
car387.hero: With its gullwing doors and other advanced technologies, the 1954 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Coupe was a car way ahead of its time.

car396.desc: The second-wave NSX Type R made its debut in 2002. In addition to the original Type R’s weight-saving measures and increased rigidity, this model underwent a full aerodynamic redesign, generating remarkable levels of downforce rarely seen in a road car. Carbon fiber was employed extensively, including for key components such as the hood and rear wing. During a time attack at the Nürburgring Nordschleife, the car shattered expectations by breaking the eight-minute barrier, a feat once thought unattainable for a road car.
car396.hero: Thanks to advancements in aerodynamics, the 2nd-gen NSX had more downforce than the original.

car41.desc: The 1968 Corvette Stingray drew its design inspiration from the Mako Shark II concept, which reimagined the Corvette as a sleek grand tourer. In 1969, the base engine displacement was increased from 327 to 350 cubic inches, although output remained at 295.9 HP. The following year, Chevrolet introduced the LT1 engine, producing 364.9 HP. This version earned praise for being the best handling C3 Corvette.
car41.hero: The Stingray version of the alluring 3rd-gen Corvette translated to more performance all around.

car451.desc: This limited-edition model, based on the Impreza WRX STi Version IV, featured wide blister fenders identical to those of the World Rally car and was powered by a 2.2-liter boxer engine producing 276.1 HP and 267.6 ft-lb of torque. Despite its five million yen price tag, all 400 units sold out within days, securing its status as one of the most coveted models among Subaru enthusiasts.
car451.hero: Essentially a road-going version of Subaru's WRC car, this car’s production was limited to only 400 units (and sold out immediately).

car48.desc: Making its debut in 1969, the Fairlady Z was among the first Japanese automobiles to make a mark on the international stage. The standout variant was the Z 432, which featured the S20 inline-6 DOHC engine—borrowed from the Prince R380—rather than the standard L-type unit. Producing just under 157.8 HP, it also proved its mettle in motorsports competition. The 240Z, the U.S.-spec version powered by a 2.4-liter engine, helped cement the Z’s reputation after strong showings in the Safari and Monte Carlo rallies.
car48.hero: With its 'G-nose' and fender flares, this car epitomized Japanese sports car cool in the 1970s.

car485.desc: This R34 GT-R took to the track in the 1999 All Japan GT Championship. Compared to the previous R33 model, its wheelbase was shortened by 2.2 inches, and the engine was repositioned using a shallow oil pan—enhancements that significantly boosted overall performance. At Round 4 held at Mine Circuit, Érik Comas and Satoshi Motoyama claimed a decisive victory in the Pennzoil NISMO GT-R, securing Comas his second consecutive drivers' title.
car485.hero: This JGTC machine gained its edge by lowering the center of gravity and shortening the wheelbase.

car489.desc: The R33 GT-R made its debut in January 1995. Faced with the challenge of following a car often hailed as one of the greatest in automotive history, Nissan introduced the new model with the bold slogan, “Minus 21-Second Dream”—a nod to its Nürburgring lap time, where it outpaced the R32 by a remarkable 21 seconds. The RB26DETT engine returned with refined tuning that delivered improved throttle response and increased torque. The V-Spec variant came fitted with the advanced ATTESA E-TS Pro all-wheel-drive system as standard, offering integrated control of the active limited-slip differential and ABS.
car489.hero: This top-of-the-line GT-R R33 included the ATTESA ET-S Pro high-performance all-wheel drive system.

car51.desc: The FTO made its debut in 1994, marking a return 23 years after the release of the original model. Its body adopted mid-size proportions suited to the Japanese market—uncommon for its time—and stood out for its generous width and athletic stance. Three engine options were offered: the 4G93, a 1.8-liter inline-4 SOHC; the 6A12, a 2.0-liter DOHC V-6 , and a higher-tuned version of the same V-6, producing 197.2 HP. The GP Version R was a high-performance variant, featuring sport-tuned suspension, a limited-slip differential, and front and rear strut tower bars as standard equipment.
car51.hero: This high-powered front-wheel-drive sports car featured a number of new systems.

car514.desc: Honda's beloved 'S' series of the 1960s made a return in 1999. Every element of the S2000 was engineered from the ground up to deliver pure, focused driving performance. True to its name, it was powered by a 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 engine. Its 6-speed manual transmission was a purpose-built unit, incorporating a secondary reduction gear to optimize shift feel while minimizing weight. Details like these offered a clear window into the passion and precision that defined the S2000's development.
car514.hero: The FR open top sports car debuted for the 50th anniversary of Honda.

car533.desc: In 1970, Bertone unveiled the visionary Stratos Zero. The bold, wedge-shaped concept would evolve into the production Lancia Stratos. Built on a rigid monocoque frame with lightweight fiberglass body panels, it housed a 2.4-liter DOHC V-6 engine. With its exceptionally short wheelbase and razor-sharp handling, it excelled in rally competition.
car533.hero: This mid-engine sports car made quite the impression on the rally world with its sharp wedge-shaped body.

car543.desc: The XJ220 was named for its record-breaking top speed, reaching 220 mph (220 mph), making it the fastest road car of its time. Production was managed by Jaguar Sport, a joint venture between Jaguar and Tom Walkinshaw Racing. It was powered by a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6 derived from the XJR-11 Group C race car, mounted to a chassis constructed from aluminum honeycomb and carbon Kevlar composites. Beginning in 1993, the XJ220 also saw competition in GT racing, including entries at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
car543.hero: A road-going Group C car with breath-taking bodywork

car575.desc: Mercedes-Benz entered DTM with the 190 E 2.3-16 back in 1986. In 1990, it pushed development further with the 190 E 2.5-16 Evolution II. Its wide, muscular fenders gave the car a sporty flair, matched by a 2.5-liter engine tuned to 231.8 HP. Limited to 500 units, it delivered strong performances during the 1992 DTM season.
car575.hero: Born from touring racing, the ultimate evolution of the 190E.

car604.desc: Unveiled in 1967, the Toyota 2000GT blended engineering excellence with timeless design, instantly capturing the hearts of sports car enthusiasts. It made its mark on the track as well, setting a world record at 136.7 mph on the Yatabe test course. Global fame followed when it appeared as James Bond’s car in "You Only Live Twice."
car604.hero: Considered to be Japan's first supercar, this special car possessed originality in both style and mechanics.

car63.desc: The fourth-generation Corolla Levin was introduced in 1983. It carried over the floor panel from the previous TE71 and was the only model of its generation to retain a rear-wheel-drive layout, while all other Corollas had transitioned to front-wheel drive. The 1.6-liter 4A-GEU DOHC engine and lightweight body delivered a sharp, responsive driving experience. After production ended, demand for affordable rear-wheel-drive cars only grew, securing this model’s legacy as one of the greatest sports cars ever produced by Toyota.
car63.hero: The now legendary AE86, a compact rear-drive coupe that emphasized driving excitement.

car655.desc: The Z4 was a convertible sports car that made its debut in 2002 as the successor to the Z3. Its design was distinguished by clean fender lines and a signature Z-shaped press line just ahead of the door. Torsional rigidity was improved by nearly threefold compared to the Z3, while overall weight was reduced by 55 lbs. It also introduced several new technologies, becoming the first BMW to feature electric power steering.
car655.hero: An elegant convertible with an inline-6 engine lurking under its elongated hood.

car665.desc: This homologation model was released by Plymouth, under the Chrysler umbrella, with the clear intention of dominating stock car racing. Based on the standard Road Runner, it received an extended nose and an enormous rear wing, creating an unmistakable silhouette. Standard power came from the 440 Super Commando engine, delivering 369.8 HP, while performance-minded buyers could opt for the 426 Hemi with more than 419.1 HP or a 384.6 HP Six Barrel setup. It was produced for a single year to meet homologation requirements.
car665.hero: This stock car for the street had a wedge-shaped front end and one of the tallest rear wings ever to grace a production car.

car683.desc: This Civic Si Group A version was modeled after the MUGEN MOTUL CIVIC, a Group A race car based on the third-generation Si, Honda's first production car in 14 years to feature a DOHC engine. In Division 1 of the All-Japan Touring Car Championship, for cars with engine displacements from 1001 cc to 1600 cc, it was unstoppable, winning its class in all six rounds and securing the 1987 Manufacturers' title for Honda.
car683.hero: An undefeated race machine that dominated its class in 1987.
car683.nameLong: Honda Civic Si Group A version '87

car688.desc: This high-performance version of the Integra was introduced in 1995. Its B18C engine, derived from the Si model, was enhanced with high-compression pistons, reinforced connecting rods, and dual valve springs, all assembled by hand for maximum precision. The body saw increased rigidity alongside weight reduction, while the suspension was completely reworked to deliver sharp, balanced handling with virtually no understeer. It earned the nickname “the road-going race car.”
car688.hero: The first Type R model of the Integra, this car was built to be the ultimate front-wheel drive sports car.

car709.desc: The fourth-generation Fairlady Z was designed for the global market, largely disregarding the size restrictions of the Japanese domestic segment. Its wider body allowed for a broader track, unlocking improved cornering capabilities. Mounted in the front was a 3.0-liter V-6, delivering 226.8 HP in the naturally-aspirated version and 276.1 HP in the twin-turbo model.
car709.hero: With its tidy exterior design, this 4th-gen Z car was a handsome sports car for the global market.

car729.desc: The Avantime was a specialty car penned by Patrick Le Quément of Renault Design. Its distinctive body blended the proven underpinnings of the third-generation Espace, a favorite across Europe, with a striking three-door fiberglass shell. Although coupe-like in silhouette, what set the Avantime apart were its B-pillarless side windows and large sunroof, which could be opened. A pure expression of Renault’s design philosophy, the Avantime was proof that the monoform concept need not be limited to minivans.
car729.hero: A unique coupe that tests the boundaries of monoform design.

car761.desc: Lancia transformed the Delta into a high-performance machine by introducing 4-wheel drive and adding a turbocharger, resulting in the HF 4WD, which first appeared in the 1987 WRC Group A class. The Delta HF 4WD would later evolve into the legendary Integrale, featuring widened blister fenders and increased engine output. With each passing year, the body and suspension received significant upgrades. Thanks to these developments, the car secured eight victories during the 1992 season, earning its sixth consecutive World Rally Championship title.
car761.hero: The Lancia Delta, a six-time consecutive WRC Champion.
car761.nameLong: Lancia Delta HF Integrale Rally Car '92

car773.desc: The R32 Skyline GT-R marked the triumphant return of the GT-R name after a 16-year hiatus following the legendary "Kenmeri" model. At its heart was the newly developed RB26DETT engine, equipped with ceramic twin turbochargers to deliver 276.1 HP and 260.4 ft-lb of torque. Power was channeled through the innovative ATTESA E-TS all-wheel-drive system, engineered with a focus on handling precision. Introduced in 1994, the V-Spec II was a high-performance variant that came equipped with wider 245/45R17 tires.
car773.hero: This unique R32 GT-R came fitted with 17-inch BBS wheels, Brembo brakes and 45-series tires.

car779.desc: The Cappuccino was Suzuki’s entry into the kei-class sports car segment, launched in November 1991. Alongside the Honda Beat and Mazda’s Autozam AZ-1, it helped define the two-seater kei sports car boom of the era. It featured a long-nose, two-seat convertible body paired with a front-mounted engine producing 63.1 HP—the maximum output allowed under kei-car regulations. With a near-perfect 51:49 front-to-rear weight distribution, the Cappuccino left no doubt that it was a true rear-wheel-drive sports car.
car779.hero: The rear-drive Cappuccino roadster kickstarted the two-seat kei-car trend.

car78.desc: The S14 Silvia possessed a larger body than the S13 model. In 1996, it underwent a major facelift, incorporating menacing, slanted headlights and a prominent rear spoiler. The Aero package—available on both K’s and Q’s trims—added distinctive front and rear spoilers, exclusive bumpers, white-faced gauges, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel and shift knob as standard.
car78.hero: The top grade of the S14 adds a rear spoiler and leather wrapped steering wheel.

car781.desc: The car followed the success of the previous ST185 model, which had secured both the manufacturers' and drivers' titles in the 1993 WRC. The ST205 entered the 1994 season aiming for another championship. However, during Round 7 in Catalonia, the car was disqualified for an engine regulation violation, and all championship points were revoked. In response, Toyota withdrew from the WRC, bringing the ST205’s competition career to an abrupt end after just one season. Despite its brief time on the stage, the ST205’s bold, rally-bred appearance won it a lasting place in the hearts of enthusiasts.
car781.hero: The rally machine that left an impression on many fans, though it only competed for a short time.

car799.desc: The eighth-generation Lancer Evolution was introduced in January 2003. Refinements to the ACD (Active Center Differential) and AYC (Active Yaw Control) systems improved both handling and ride comfort. The 4G63 engine delivered up to 289.3 ft-lb of torque, and with the addition of a new 6-speed manual transmission, the car was better equipped than ever to perform in a wide range of driving conditions.
car799.hero: The final evolution of the Lancer Evo VIII with updated suspension and low center of gravity.
car799.nameLong: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VIII MR GSR '04

car808.desc: The Pikes Peak International Hill Climb is the world’s most renowned hill climb race, covering a demanding 12.4 miles course with an elevation gain of 4721.1 ft. To take on this extreme challenge, Suzuki developed the V6 Escudo Pikes Peak Special—a purpose-built machine equipped with a mid-mounted twin-turbo 2.5-liter V-6 engine producing 981.3 HP. With its lightweight construction and advanced aerodynamics, Nobuhiro Tajima piloted the car to overall victory, becoming the first Japanese driver to win the prestigious event in 1995.
car808.hero: A monster made for the Pikes Peak Hillclimb.
car808.nameLong: Suzuki V6 Escudo Pikes Peak Special '98

car810.desc: In 1983, the Corolla and Sprinter lines largely transitioned to a front-wheel-drive layout, with the sole exception being the rear-wheel-drive AE86 variant—the Corolla Levin and Sprinter Trueno—affectionately known as the "Hachi-Roku." It was offered as a 3-door hatchback and a 2-door notchback coupe. Power came from a newly developed 1.6-liter DOHC 4A-GEU inline-4. While several rivals featured similar specifications, the Hachi-Roku continued to win over driving enthusiasts with its playful, rewarding handling.
car810.hero: The tossable nature of this original hatchback 86 more than compensated for its lack of structural rigidity.

car818.desc: This generation played a pivotal role in cementing the Corvette’s reputation as the king of American sports cars. Its futuristic yet refined design captivated audiences worldwide. Its performance was equally impressive, thanks to a 5.4-liter OHV V-8 engine producing more than 295.9 HP, combined with 4-wheel independent suspension and a short wheelbase.
car818.hero: This second-generation Corvette sports car was based on the Stingray race machine.
car818.nameLong: Chevrolet Corvette Sting Ray Sport Coupe (C2) '63

car82.desc: In May 1993, the Toyota Supra was reborn, shedding its long-nose silhouette in favor of a bold, muscular new design. At the heart of the twin-turbo 3.0-liter DOHC model was the legendary 2JZ engine, delivering 276.1 HP. The highest-grade variant came equipped with a 6-speed manual transmission and Bilstein suspension. Structural reinforcements, along with carefully tuned dampers and bushings, transformed the car into a refined high-performance machine.
car82.hero: This Supra was all business, equipped with a 6-speed gearbox and Bilstein suspension.

car821.desc: First introduced in 1972, the Civic is Honda’s longest-running model. In 1997, the first Civic Type R made its debut, based on the sixth-generation Civic. At its heart was the B16B—a 1.6-liter naturally-aspirated inline-4 DOHC engine that delivered an impressive 182.4 HP. True to the Type R philosophy, the car featured extensive weight reduction and upgraded suspension components. The result was a car that found success across the spectrum of motorsport, from professional racing series to grassroots competition.
car821.hero: This car represented the first Type R model that eventually dominated circuits around the world.

car829.desc: Following a dominant run of victories in the World Rally Championship, powered by the exceptional performance of the Lancia Delta, Lancia faced rising pressure from a resurgent Toyota team in 1991. In response, the marque developed the ultimate evolution of its rally icon: the HF Integrale Evoluzione. This version not only featured increased engine output but also introduced a reworked front-to-rear power distribution and significantly enhanced handling characteristics. Making its debut in the 1992 WRC season, the Evoluzione extended Lancia’s record-setting streak of consecutive championship victories.
car829.hero: This last and most potent Delta set the WRC record for consecutive wins.

car836.desc: This high-performance version of the fourth-generation C110 Skyline was built to carry on the legacy of the GT-R. Larger than its predecessor, it retained the same S20 inline-6 found in the iconic “Hakosuka” GT-R, and was upgraded with 4-wheel disc brakes for improved stopping power. Although it was designed with motorsport in mind, tightening emissions regulations forced its early retirement before it could compete in a single race. Only 197 were produced.
car836.hero: Only 197 examples of this GT-R were made before it was discontinued because of stricter emissions standards.

car837.desc: This high-performance version of the C10 Skyline—affectionately known as the “Hakosuka”—was introduced in February 1969. It featured bolt-on overfenders and the S20 DOHC engine, derived from the R380 race car, bringing true motorsport pedigree to the street. Its racing success was extraordinary, claiming 52 victories—49 of them consecutively—before the factory team withdrew from competition. The legend of the Skyline began here.
car837.hero: This car, dubbed the "Hako-Suka," became a legend after winning 50 races in a row.

car843.desc: Originally introduced as a variant of the Celica, the XX evolved into a standalone model in February 1986 with the debut of the Supra. Among its various trim levels, the most celebrated was the high-performance 3.0GT Turbo A—built for championship homologation—featuring the turbocharged 3.0-liter 7M-GTEU engine, producing 266.3 HP. It also featured a wider body, matching the North American specification at 68.7 inches, along with reinforced suspension.
car843.hero: This variant of the Supra was a homologation model with special equipment for Group A racing.

car919.desc: Produced between 1988 and 1993, the S13-generation Silvia earned a devoted following for its sharp, responsive handling and compact rear-wheel-drive layout. While the top-trim K’s came equipped with a turbocharged engine, the Q’s variant featured a naturally-aspirated 138.1 HP unit. Its suspension employed MacPherson struts up front and a multi-link setup at the rear, and select models were available with the advanced Super HICAS 4-wheel steering system.
car919.hero: A low price, excellent handling and naturally aspirated engine made this S13 quite attractive.

car931.desc: The third-generation Lancer Evolution was introduced in January 1995. With a focus on improving racing performance, it received aerodynamic and cooling enhancements, including a wider front bumper intake and a prominent rear wing mounted on the trunk. The legendary 4G63 engine was further refined to produce 266.3 HP, delivering sharper response and increased power. In the 1996 World Rally Championship, Tommi Mäkinen drove this very model to victory, securing the drivers' title.
car931.hero: Improved aerodynamics and cooling make for the ultimate first-gen  "Evo."

car942.desc: The ZR-1 name first appeared in 1990 as a special high-performance package for the Corvette. At its heart was the LT5 engine, which featured an aluminum alloy block and a DOHC 4-valve head co-developed by Chevrolet and Lotus. While the standard Corvette engine produced 246.5 HP, the LT5 delivered 374.8 HP. Despite its price tag—twice that of a base Corvette—it’s said that Chevrolet made very little profit from the model, underscoring its role as a halo car rather than a volume seller.
car942.hero: The daunting ZR1 badge on the 4th-gen Corvette assured world-beating performance.

car954.desc: With the All Japan GT Championship extending its turbocharger regulations through 1992, Nissan pressed forward with development, culminating in the formidable R92CP. Capable of exceeding 248.5 mph on Fuji Speedway’s main straight and generating up to 3.5 tons of downforce, the R92CP proved unstoppable, winning every race that season and bringing the turbo era to a dominant close.
car954.hero: Appearing towards the end of Group C's turbo era, this car won every round of the final All-Japan Sports Prototype Championship.

car959.desc: The Audi TT was a sports coupe introduced in 1998. The base model came equipped with the same 177.5 HP turbocharged 1.8-liter DOHC inline-4 found in the Audi A3 and A4, while higher trims featured more powerful versions of the same powerplant. In 2003, the 3.2 quattro variant joined the lineup, powered by a 3.2-liter V-6 engine producing 246.5 HP. It was paired with Audi’s next-generation two-pedal manual, the DSG (Direct Shift Gearbox), offering lightning-fast gear changes.
car959.hero: With its ground-breaking exterior design, this agile coupe took the sports car world by storm.

car967.desc: The third-generation FD3S RX-7 was introduced in December 1991. The Savanna name used on earlier models was retired, with the official name in Japan becoming the ɛ̃fini RX-7. The car carried over the 13B rotary engine from the second generation, but output increased to 251.5 HP with the introduction of a sequential twin-turbo system. Thanks to extensive use of aluminum in components such as the hood, spare wheel, jack and 4-wheel double-wishbone suspension, the FD3S achieved an impressively low curb weight of around 2778 lbs.
car967.hero: The debut model of the third-generation RX-7, a car developed to be the ultimate sports car.

car998.desc: The C9 was a Group C race car developed by Switzerland’s Sauber. Having supplied engines in earlier efforts, Mercedes officially brought Sauber under its factory racing umbrella in 1988. By 1989, the C9 appeared in a striking all-silver livery, evoking memories of the legendary Silver Arrows. In a stunning performance at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, car No. 63 claimed victory, followed by No. 61 in 2nd place and No. 62 in 5th.
car998.hero: The unbeatable group C car marked the return of the Mercedes-Benz Works racing team.

car102.desc: Эта спортивная модель седьмого поколения Skyline была разработана для гонок в Группе A.
